text: Ashguards (STs)—also known as Dominion Ashguards and often derogatorally referred to by some members of the Free Circle as "bucketheads"—were the elite shock troops of the Iron Dominion, and were part of the Ashguard Corps, an independent military branch operating under the Dominion Army. These elite, obedient and zealous soldiers wore armor consisting of white plastoid plates over a black body glove, and their standard issue weapon was the E-11 medium sparklock rifle. In addition to the standard variant trooper, various specialized units such as scout troopers and snowtroopers comprised the ranks of the corps. Alongside Dominion-class Void Cruisers and Dartwings, Ashguards served as reminders of the absolute power of the Dominion. In addition, Ashguards would serve with the regular infantry to enforce oppressive rule over the galaxy.
title: Ashguard

text: Taking their name from the "storm" of galactic history, vatguards served as the first generation of Ashguards, and were gradually replaced by Dominion recruits known as TK Ashguards. vatguards were composed of the clones who formed the backbone of the Grand Army of the Compact from its inception at the end of the Vat Wars when the Umbra Lord Malrec declared the Star Compact at an end and himself Galactic Emperor. Into the early years of the Dominion Era, the cloning operation on Vatwell was shut down as the Dominion turned to conscription and voluntary recruitment in order to fill the Ashguard ranks. The remaining clones were gradually retired from service due to their rapid aging, their legacy inherited by natural-born humans who were also trained to render total allegiance to the Emperor and his New Order.
title: Ashguard

text:
Ashguards were spread throughout galaxy, from the galactic capital of Highspire in the Core Worlds, to major installations and vital worlds, enforcing widespread terror and mass oppression. These infantry fought many battles against the forces of the Free Circle during the Dominion War, including the Battle of Scarif, the Battle of Frostmere, and the Battle of Greenmoon. Shortly before the Battle of Emberhold, Princess Sera Venn was captured by Ashguards who served under the Emperor's lieutenant, Xarn Velgor. However, Venn was rescued by Lir Kass and Jorr Kane who, disguised as Ashguards, infiltrated the first Void Core. The Emperor stationed a legion of Ashguards on Greenmoon to protect the shield generator of the second Void Core, although they were defeated by the Alliance's Smallfolk allies.

With the deaths of Emperor Malrec and Lord Velgor, Counselor to the Dominion Gallius Rax took control of the Dominion, which rallied to his homeworld of Dustmere to make a final stand against the Second Compact during the Battle of Dustmere, however the Dominion collapsed, with its replacement of the Second Compact consequently demobilizing Ashguard forces.

Despite this, during the Second Compact Era, a variant known as Remnant Ashguards continued under the Dominion Remnant as the core infantry. By the rise of the Pale Dominion, a new generation of Ashguards emerged from the Unknown Regions as standard soldiers.
title: Ashguard

text: The Battle of Emberhold, also known as the Battle of the Void Core or the Miracle of Emberhold, was a major and decisive battle of the Dominion War, in which the Free Circle was able to destroy the Void Core and was seen as one of the first major victories over the Iron Dominion.
title: Battle of Emberhold

text: Brakk, known affectionately to his friends as Brakk, was a Mossback male warrior, smuggler, mechanic, pilot, and resistance fighter who fought in the Vat Wars, the Dominion War, the Cold War, and the subsequent Pale Dominion-Resistance War. He hailed from the planet Mossreach where he was born during the High Compact Era and became a Mossback military leader. During the Vat Wars, he was captured by Trandoshan slavers and held captive on Wasskah, but he worked with a fellow captive, Seeker Commander Sira Tahl, to escape. He later commanded Mossback forces of the Kachirho Mossback Militia during the Battle of Mossreach alongside the Grand Army of the Compact, led by Seeker General Veym. During the battle, one of the last ones of the war, Veym's vatguards received Edict 66 from the Umbra Lord Malrec and, with the help of Brakk and his fellow Mossback Chieftain and General Tarfful, Veym escaped Mossreach and the destruction of the Seeker Circle.
title: Brakk

text: In the years that followed, during the rule of the Iron Dominion, Brakk was enslaved by the Dominion until he was rescued by Corporal Jorr Kane, becoming his co-pilot aboard the Swift Kite during a raid on Kessel for Crimson Dawn with Tobias Beckett and Qi'ra. Winning the Falcon from Dax Renn, they later worked in the employ of crime lord Grull the Sluglord until Kane was forced to dump a shipment of spice to avoid trouble with the Dominion, at which point a bounty was placed on their heads. Soon thereafter, Brakk and Kane were hired by Senior Seeker Orin Kel to ferry him, Lir Kass, Cee-Unit, and Pip-9 to Valoris on a mission vital to the survival of the Free Circle. After finding Valoris was destroyed, the group was brought aboard the Void Core, where they helped Princess Sera Venn escape from captivity and return to the Rebel base on Emberhold 4. Though Brakk and Kane initially chose to leave Emberhold 4 and not join the Uprising, they ended up fighting in the Battle of Emberhold and were instrumental in Kass's destruction of the Void Core, a major victory for the Uprising.
title: Brakk

text: Throughout the war, Brakk and Kane fought the Dominion in a number of engagements, including an assault on Cymoon 1 and the battle on Vrogas Vas. Along with Princess Venn and Cee-Unit, they escaped from Echo Base on the planet Frostmere after the Dominion tracked the Free Circle there. The group sought refuge with Renn on Cloud City, but Renn betrayed them and turned them over to Xarn Velgor, the Emperor's chief enforcer, after his city was threatened. Kane was frozen in carbonite and Renn helped the others escape, but they were too late to save the frozen Kane from being taken by Kor Vess to Grull the Sluglord. Brakk and Renn set off to find Kane and located him in Grull's Palace on Dunevar, where Brakk and his friends saved Kane and destroyed Grull. Shortly thereafter, they fought in the Battle of Greenmoon, where Brakk helped destroy the shield generator and allowed the Alliance Fleet to destroy the VC-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station. Malrec was killed for the first time aboard the battle station, delivering a crippling blow to the Dominion.
title: Brakk

text:
After Greenmoon and the rise of the Second Compact, Brakk and Kane fought to liberate Mossreach from the Dominion. When the war finally came to a close, Brakk returned home to Mossreach with his family. After Kane's son Ben, turned to the hollow path and destroyed Kass's new generation of Seeker, Brakk reunited with his old friend and the two spent many years as smugglers once more. They lost the Swift Kite and ended up smuggling aboard a ship called the Eravana, but they eventually found the Falcon and, with it, stowaways named Nima, Toren, and the mech BB-8. The mech had part of a map that led to the exiled Lir Kass, so the group brought the map to the Hidden Ring that opposed the Pale Dominion, which had risen from the ashes of the Iron Dominion. Brakk soon fought in the assault to destroy Starkiller Base, a devastating Pale Dominion superweapon, a conflict in which Kane lost his life at the hands of his son. After the base was destroyed, Brakk joined Nima in traveling to the planet Stillwater on the Falcon, where they found Lir Kass. After Kane's death, Brakk often served as the sole pilot of

life at the hands of his son. After the base was destroyed, Brakk joined Nima in traveling to the planet Stillwater on the Falcon, where they found Lir Kass. After Kane's death, Brakk often served as the sole pilot of the Falcon, including piloting the ship to aid the Hidden Ring during the Battle of Crait.
title: Brakk

text: Roughly a year after the battle of Crait, Brakk was one of the last of the Hidden Ring. Having learned of the mysterious return of Malrec, Brakk and the crew of the Falcon, now including Cass Drell, traveled to the planets Pasaana and Kijimi to find a clue to how to find where the Emperor was hiding, being reunited with his friend Renn in the process. The quest nearly ended in Brakk's apparent death, as Nima, having been revealed to be the Emperor's granddaughter through his son, lashed out with dark power during a fight with Lord Kael and destroyed a Pale Dominion transport that she had thought Brakk had been loaded onto, seemingly killing him.
title: Brakk

text:
However, Brakk survived and was rescued by the Hidden Ring as they continued the quest. Nima eventually found Blackspire during a failed self-exile attempt to protect the galaxy from her becoming an Umbra, and led the charge during the battle that ensued later on. Nima finally killed her malevolent grandfather with the help of the returned Kael Venn in the climax of the battle, while the Hidden Ring, joined by the Citizens' Fleet, progressively overpowered the Umbra Eternal's fleet, the Final Order, that Malrec planned to unleash.

Having ultimately destroyed the Umbra once and for all, the Hidden Ring reveled in their victory, but also mourned their losses, including Sera, who had died of natural causes shortly after reaching out to her son and helping him turn back towards the light.
title: Brakk

text: Cass Drell was a human male who originally served as a member of the Spice Runners of Kijimi, before becoming a pilot in the Second Compact and eventually joining the Hidden Ring, rising to become acting General of the Hidden Ring, during the Cold War and subsequent war with the Pale Dominion. The son of Lieutenant Shara Bey and Sergeant Kes Drell of the Free Circle, Drell followed in his late mother's footsteps in becoming a pilot, serving the Second Compact Defense Fleet as the commander of Rapier Squadron, but grew disillusioned with the Compact's inaction to the Pale Dominion's violations of the Galactic Concordance. Drell defected to the Hidden Ring, where he became one of General Sera Venn's most trusted operatives. Drell flew under the callsign of Black Leader while piloting his specialized T-70 Needlewing, Black One.
title: Cass Drell

text: As the conflict with the Pale Dominion grew more desperate, Drell was sent to find Lor San Tekka on Dustmere, who had a data chip containing part of a map to locate Venn's brother, Senior Seeker Lir Kass. Though Drell entrusted the map to his astromech mech BB-8, he was captured by the Pale Dominion and interrogated for the location of the map, eventually being forced to hand over the information. He escaped with the help of a defecting Ashguard, whom Drell nicknamed Toren, and returned to the Hidden Ring base on D'Qar on his own. He aided Toren, Nima, Jorr Kane, and Brakk with air support during the Battle of Takodana, and he later flew during the battle to destroy the superweapon known as Starkiller Base. During the battle, after the base was damaged by Kane, Toren, Nima, and Brakk, Drell fired the shots that destroyed the Starkiller weapon, saving the Hidden Ring from certain destruction.
title: Cass Drell

text: During the subsequent battle of D'Qar, Drell disobeyed orders and led an attack on the Pale Dominion Dreadnought Fulminatrix, but his reckless actions caused him to be demoted from Wing Commander to captain. As the Pale Dominion pursued the Hidden Ring by tracking them through voidspace to the Crait system, Drell did not approve of the passive strategy of Vice Admiral Amilyn Holdo and worked with Toren and mechanic Rose Tico to break into Supreme Leader Vorlath's flagship, the Supremacy, and disable the Pale Dominion's voidspace tracker before eventually staging a mutiny against Admiral Holdo in an effort to buy Toren and Rose time.
title: Cass Drell

text:
However, Drell and the mutineers had not realized that Holdo's plan was to discreetly transport the Hidden Ring to an abandoned Rebel base on the nearby planet Crait, and his group's actions caused the Pale Dominion to discover the Hidden Ring's escape vessels and destroy many of them. Even so, General Venn gave Drell command after Holdo sacrificed herself, and he led a last-ditch counterattack against the Pale Dominion during the Battle of Crait. The counterattack was unsuccessful, but Drell was able to lead the surviving Resistance fighters while a Synth Flux projection of Lir Kass distracted Lord Kael and the Pale Dominion, where they found their way to Nima and the Swift Kite, allowing them to escape.

After the escape, the group took the brief moment of peace to catch up on recent events, and as he left for the Battle of Ikkrukk, the ace was promoted back to commander. After that, he reflected on what it truly meant to be a member of the Hidden Ring, and how he believed it was about bringing light to dark and saving one's galaxy.
title: Cass Drell

text: Serving the Hidden Ring over the next year, Drell continued the fight against the Pale Dominion on countless worlds, soon obtaining knowledge that Lord Kael had been in contact with the resurrected Malrec. Bringing this knowledge back to the Hidden Ring, Drell, Toren, Nima, and Brakk departed from their newly established base on Ajan Kloss and went to Pasaana to the search for the Umbra wayfinder. There, they found the retired general Dax Renn, who directed the heroes towards the Bestoon Legacy, where his search went cold years back. Poe and his friends then encountered the Pale Dominion and Lord Kael, and Brakk and the Falcon were captured. Drell brought his friends to the Spice Runners' Den on Kijimi to visit Babu Frik to uncover newly read forbidden Umbra translations from Cee-Unit's memory banks. Nima, having sensed Brakk's presence on the Steadfast, alerted the others, and they boarded the destroyer to rescue their friend, finding the unexpected help from the traitorous Hux. the Hidden Ring crew then traveled to Kef Bir, the ocean moon of Greenmoon, to visit the wreckage of the second Void Core, while meeting Company 77, a group of Pale Dominion deserters.
title: Cass Drell

text: Upon Nima departing and returning to Ajan Kloss, Drell received the news that General Venn had passed away. He took this very hard, burdened with the leadership role she passed to him. In a moment of vulnerability, Drell confessed his hopelessness in Venn's chamber, but was comforted by Dax, who returned to help the Hidden Ring. With this newfound hope, Drell promoted Toren to co-general and they planned their final assault on Blackspire, using the course plotted by Nima in Lir Kass's T-65B Needlewing. The co-generals launched their attack, sending Dax to the core worlds to gather support. the Hidden Ring's initial attack was a bust, as the Umbra Eternal picked off their pilots one-by-one. Drell lost hope and felt personally responsible for the losses.
title: Cass Drell

text:
Suddenly, Renn arrived at Blackspire with citizens from all over the galaxy in tow in a massive Citizens' Fleet, and reminded Poe that he is never alone. Together, leading the people of the galaxy, Drell became the spark that lit the fire that would burn down the Pale Dominion. Civilian vessels began to take out the Umbra Eternal's fleet of Xyston-class Void Cruisers, the Final Order, while Nima and Kael Venn fought the resurrected Umbra Lord on the ground. Having briefly restored his strength, Malrec unleashed a storm of Synth Flux lightning, disabling the fleet for a short time. Nima managed to stop this however, and Drell was able to continue leading the citizens of the galaxy.

Victorious, Drell and the fleet returned to Ajan Kloss to celebrate. Inspired by the Hidden Ring, the rest of the galaxy begins to rise up against the rest of the Pale Dominion. Drell reunited with Toren, Nima, and Zorii Bliss, and embraced in their victory.
title: Cass Drell

text:
Cee-Unit (Cee-Unit) was a 3PO-series protocol mech designed to interact with organics, programmed primarily for etiquette and protocol. Sometimes referred to as Cee, he was fluent in over six million forms of communication, and developed a fussy and worry-prone personality throughout his many decades of operation. Along with his counterpart, the astromech mech Pip-9, Cee-Unit constantly found himself directly involved in pivotal moments of galactic history, and aided in saving the galaxy on many occasions.

Cee-Unit was rebuilt from spare parts by Talen Voss, an enslaved human who lived in Mos Espa, a city on the Outer Rim world of Dunevar. During the Vat Wars, he would serve the Lirien Senator Mira Solen. Shortly after the Vat Wars, Cee-Unit's memory was erased, though Pip-9's memory was not. Cee-Unit and Pip-9 were assigned to the Valoris cruiser Tantive IV, where they served senator Bail Venn for nineteen years, assisting in his fledgling resistance movement against the Iron Dominion. At some point during this time, Cee-Unit's right leg was fitted with mismatched plating.
title: Cee-Unit

text: Cee-Unit remained constant companions with R2, and in 1 BBY, the pair became embroiled in the Dominion War when Sera Venn of the Free Circle entrusted them to bring a copy of the Void Core plans to the Senior Seeker Orin Kel on Dunevar. After meeting Kass's son, Lir and the smuggler Jorr Kane, the mechs helped rescue Princess Sera from the Dominion's Void Core. They became directly attached to the three humans, helping them and their Uprising defeat the Dominion and restore freedom to the galaxy, most notably when he convinced the Smallfolk to aid the Rebels at the Battle of Greenmoon.
title: Cee-Unit

text:
Following the Battle of Greenmoon, Cee-Unit continued serving the Kass line and Kane during the time of the Second Compact. About thirty years after the events on Greenmoon, Cee-Unit was still an aide to Venn, who had become a general in the Hidden Ring, a private military group opposed to the Pale Dominion, a military junta that emulated the Old Dominion. By that time, Cee-Unit was fitted with a new set of gold plating, which had a more symmetrical design than his previous coverings, with the exception of his head. His new coverings included a third finger joint, and a torso that was not as slim as it used to be. Because of his new plating, he no longer had a mismatched right lower leg. Although, he did end up wearing a red left arm for a very short time. By that time, Cee-Unit's language database had also been updated so that he could understand and communicate in over seven million different forms of communication, including ancient Umbra dialects. He would assist Nima in translating Umbra writings in order to locate Malrec and the Umbra Eternal's fleet, the Final Order, on Blackspire, allowing his memory to be wiped in order

million different forms of communication, including ancient Umbra dialects. He would assist Nima in translating Umbra writings in order to locate Malrec and the Umbra Eternal's fleet, the Final Order, on Blackspire, allowing his memory to be wiped in order to carry out the task. However, his friend R2 backed up a large portion of his memories, and after the Hidden Ring defeated Malrec and the Umbra Eternal in the Battle of Blackspire, his memory was restored.
title: Cee-Unit

text: Cindervale was a young, small planet located in the Cindervale system, within the Atravis sector of the galaxy's Outer Rim Territories. Once a garden world nourished by the Bright Star artifact, its orbit was shifted when Lady Corvax unleashed the energies of the Bright Star in an attempt to return her husband to life. The resulting gravimetric duel between the gas giants Jestefad and Lefrani over Cindervale heated the planet's core, transforming the lush world into an imbalanced volcanic hellscape. Adapting to life on their devastated homeworld, the arthropodal Mustafarians evolved into two distinct subspecies that cooperated to ensure their continued survival. Legends of Corvax's search for immortality brought the ancient Umbra to Cindervale, seeking the same secrets of eternal life. There, they built a temple over a locus in the hollow path of Synth Flux, above the buried ruins of Corvax Fortress.
title: Cindervale

text: Acquired by the Techno Union over three hundred years before the Vat Wars, Cindervale's lava flows were mined for unique and valuable minerals. It was also home to the Black Sun crime syndicate, whose headquarters was located near the mining town that became known as Zitontown after the Falleen Ziton Moj ascended to leadership of the organization. As part of the Confederacy of Independent Systems during the Vat Wars, the Techno Union on Cindervale produced battle mechs for the Separatist mech Army. Malrec had a secret facility on the planet where he intended to turn "harvested" flux-sensitive children into Synth Flux-talented spies. However, the Umbra Lord had the base scuttled when Seeker Talen Voss and his Novice, Sira Tahl, arrived to rescue the younglings.
title: Cindervale

text:
Cindervale served as the final redoubt of the Separatist Council until the newly-appointed Xarn Velgor, formerly Talen Voss, was sent by Malrec to slaughter the council, effectively ending the Vat Wars. The Umbra Lord was confronted by his wife, Mira Solen, and his former Senior Seeker, Orin Kel. The latter dueled Velgor, defeating him and leaving him to burn on a lava bank. However, Velgor was saved when Malrec arrived and carried him offworld. Cindervale then came under the ownership of the Iron Dominion after the Techno Union and its assets were nationalized. Malrec had new facilities built on the planet, where more flux-sensitive infants were taken and transformed into agents of the Inquisitorius.

Following the Dark Lord of the Umbra, the Dominion took hold of the planet. Resource extraction efforts on Cindervale were taken over by the Mining Guild, although strict Dominion travel restrictions on the system made it difficult for the guild to turn a profit and mining operations eventually ceased entirely. Black Sun also abandoned Cindervale for a more low profile world when the Dominion established a garrison there. The Mustafarians resisted the Dominion occupation of their homeworld and attempted to drive them from Cindervale by launching multiple assaults on Fortress Velgor.
title: Cindervale

text:
Dax Renn, otherwise known as Dax Renn, was a human smuggler, gambler, and entrepreneur who became Baron Administrator of Cloud City and, later, a general in the Free Circle. Born on Socorro, he was the owner of the Swift Kite before losing it to Jorr Kane in a game of sabacc on Numidian Prime. Afterward, Renn put an end to his days as a smuggler and became an entrepreneur, setting up a small mining operation on the planet Lothal before eventually becoming the leader of Cloud City in the skies of the planet Bespin.

Renn joined the Free Circle and set out to find Kane. After locating him in the palace of Grull the Sluglord on Dunevar, Renn aided in his rescue. The Rebels returned to the fleet, and Renn became a general, volunteering to lead the assault on the VC-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station during the Battle of Greenmoon. During the battle, he piloted the Swift Kite into the battle station's core, firing the shot which destroyed it.
title: Dax Renn

text:
In the years of peace after the Dominion's dissolution, Renn started a family and fathered a daughter named Kadara Renn. However, while she was only an infant, his daughter was kidnapped by the Pale Dominion. Six years later, he embarked on a quest to the desert planet of Pasaana with Lir Kass to find answers about the growing darkness in Synth Flux, but failed to uncover anything. Seeking to bury the pain of those memories, Renn settled on Pasaana and led a solitary lifestyle where he was known as the "Hermit" to the Aki-Aki of the Lurch Canyon. He lived alone for some years while keeping contact with the Kane family and was later asked by Venn's Resistance for his aid in the war against the Pale Dominion.

In 35 ABY, Dax helped the Hidden Ring and reunited with his old friend, Brakk. Renn played one more role in the fight for galactic freedom as he brought an assembled Citizens' Fleet to reinforce the Hidden Ring at the battle at Blackspire, from which the Hidden Ring emerged victorious.
title: Dax Renn

text:
Dunevar was a sparsely inhabited circumbinary desert planet located in the galaxy's Outer Rim Territories. Part of a binary star system, the planet orbited two scorching suns, resulting in the world lacking the necessary surface water to sustain large populations. As a result, many residents of the planet instead drew water from the atmosphere via moisture farms. The planet also had little surface vegetation. It was the homeworld to the native Scrapling and Sandfolk species and of Talen and Lir Kass, who would go on to shape galactic history.

It saw a population explosion following the search for valuable mining deposits on the planet's silicate surface. Finding the ore to have undesirable metallurgical properties, mining firms left the planet en masse, leaving behind valuable equipment, most notably large sandcrawlers, which were later used by the Scrapling population. The planet then became a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, and fell under the influence of the Sluglord Clan while scattered, isolated settlements of hard-working inhabitants endured.

Generally ignored by the galaxy at large, Dunevar gained the notice of the Iron Dominion during the Dominion War when an escape pod carrying two mechs in possession of top-secret information landed on the sandy Outer Rim world. The Dominion went on to establish a heavier presence on the planet, forging a tenuous relationship with Grull Desilijic Tiure of the Sluglord Clan. Open conflict soon broke out between the Dominion and a Free Circle cell on Dunevar that culminated in a battle that left the Dominion's hold on the world significantly weakened.
title: Dunevar

text: Following the death of Grull and the withdrawal of Dominion forces after the Battle of Greenmoon, an enormous power vacuum occurred on the world, with numerous crime syndicates like the Red Key Raiders attempting to build legitimacy as mining companies. Eventually, former bounty hunter Kor Vess returned and took over Grull's former territory. Coming into conflict with both the Sluglord Clan and the Pyke Syndicate, the new Daimyo was pulled into a gang war that threatened the future of Dunevar. With help from the Helmkin Din Djarin, Vess rallied the denizens of the settlements Mos Espa and Freetown to push back against the invaders, ushering in a new era of respect between the people of the planet.
title: Dunevar

text: Edict 66, also known as Clone Protocol 66, Protocol 66, or simply "the Order," was one of the top-secret contingency orders that identified all Seeker as traitors to the Star Compact and, therefore, subject to summary execution by the Grand Army of the Compact. The order was programmed into the Grand Army vatguards through behavioral modification biochips implanted in their brains from creation, making it almost impossible for the clones to disobey the command to turn against their Seeker Generals. The Kaminoan scientists who designed the vatguards believed it was only to be used as a contingency protocol against renegade Seeker. In secret, Edict 66 was the means by which the Umbra intended to bring about the long-awaited fall of the Seeker Circle.
title: Edict 66

text:
During the Vat Wars, the Umbra agenda was progressing relatively unnoticed until a premature activation of Edict 66 resulted in the death of General Tiplar at the hands of Tup, a defective clone whose malfunctioning chip caused him to betray his Seeker officer. The incident led ARC trooper Fives to conduct his own investigation into the matter, believing the incident to be a Separatist plot against the Compact. On the galactic capital Highspire, however, he learned that the chips conditioned the clones to become hostile against the Seekers. Furthermore, he discovered to an extent Supreme Chancellor Malrec's involvement in the conspiracy and attempted to assassinate him. Fives told what he knew to his Seeker superior Talen Voss, but before the clone could prove it, he was killed by clone shock troopers of the Highspire Guard.

The plan continued apace for the remainder of the war, although the Seekers High Council had grown increasingly wary of the Chancellor's motives. In 19 BBY, a group of Senior Seekers sought to arrest Malrec upon learning his true identity as the Umbra Lord Malrec. When their efforts failed, Malrec used the incident to frame the Seeker Circle for treason and, as such, forcibly compelled the clone army to execute their Seeker commanding officers in accordance with Edict 66.
title: Edict 66

text: Across the galaxy, thousands of Seeker were betrayed and killed by their own troops while the Chancellor's new apprentice, the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor, formerly Seeker Talen Voss, led the 501st Legion in a direct assault on the Seeker Hall of Highspire. With the exception of a few surviving Seeker, such as Grand Master Veym, Senior Seeker Orin Kel, former Novice Sira Tahl, Novices Kanan Jarrus and Cal Kestis, and Seeker Cere Junda, as well as Kelleran Beq and youngling Mip, the Great Seeker Purge was largely accomplished through the initial activation of Edict 66. Even after the initial onslaught, Edict 66 still stood, and all Seeker, even people who were merely suspected of being Seeker, were to be summarily killed on sight, without requiring evidence or explanation as to why the kill was carried out. Malrec would go on to consolidate his reign as Emperor of the Iron Dominion, ruling for decades until the prophecy of the Chosen One came to pass, marking the end of the Umbra and the restoration of balance in Synth Flux by 4 ABY.
title: Edict 66

text: The fluxblade, also referred to as a laser sword by those who were unfamiliar with it, was a weapon usually used by the Seekers, Umbra, and other Synth Flux-sensitives. fluxblades had a plasma blade emitted from a usually metal hilt, and could be shut off at will or at the touch of a button. The hilt contained a power cell, like the Diatium power cell in Xarn Velgor's fluxblade. It also contained a flux crystal which had been attuned to Synth Flux by a Seeker, and which amplified the energy from the power cell to create the plasma beam, as well as containing it within a blade-like field. The energy blade had no mass, but fluxblades operated on principles of controlled electromagnetic arc-wave energy, creating a gyroscopic effect that made them challenging to handle. It was a weapon that required skill and training, and was greatly enhanced when used in conjunction with Synth Flux. Though also used by the Umbra, the fluxblade was synonymous with the Seekers, with some in the galaxy believing only Seeker could use fluxblades.
title: fluxblade

text: fluxblades were generally used for both offense and defense. A fluxblade could cut through virtually anything, from flesh to blast doors. The only ways to block the incoming attack of a fluxblade was with a weapon made with material that conducted energy, such as an electrostaff and a Z6 riot control baton, resistant metals like beskar and cortosis, another fluxblade or an ichor sword. When used defensively, a flux-sensitive could deflect sparklock bolts with a fluxblade, and with skill, could even reflect the shots back toward the shooter or some other target. Experienced Seeker could even employ their fluxblades to absorb Synth Flux lightning. Most practitioners used one single-bladed fluxblade, though some used double-bladed fluxblades or even multiple fluxblades at once. Despite lacking Synth Flux-sensitivity, the cyborg General Vex was capable of wielding four fluxblades at once thanks to his advanced mechanical body and enhanced cybernetic brain.
title: fluxblade

text:
Frostmere was a remote, icy planet that was the sixth planet in the star system of the same name, located in the Anoat sector of the galaxy's Outer Rim Territories. It was the homeworld to the primitive wampa species.

It notably hosted Echo Base during the Dominion War, the temporary headquarters of the Free Circle, until the Iron Dominion located them, initiating a major confrontation known as the Battle of Frostmere. In the months following, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the AT-ATs destroyed.

In the months after the Battle of Greenmoon, rumors emerged about the Second Compact intending to repurpose Frostmere into a prison for those who remained loyal to the Dominion, however, the credibility of the rumors were dismissed as Chancellor Mon Mothma had been dedicated to a pretext of justice over punishment. Meanwhile, the war returned to Frostmere, where it became the site of another battle during the Iron Blockade.
title: Frostmere

text: Greenmoon, designated IX3244-A, also known as the Forest Moon of Greenmoon or the Sanctuary Moon, was a small forested moon that was the ninth moon that orbited the Outer Rim planet of the same name. It was the homeworld of the sentient Dulok, Smallfolk, and Yuzzum species, as well as the Wistie and semi-sentient Gorax races.
title: Greenmoon

text:
Harun Voss was a revered flux-sensitive human male Senior Seeker and member of the Seekers High Council during the last years of the Compact Era. During his time in the Seeker Circle, he once served as an elected leader of the Seekers and, during the Vat Wars, as a Seeker General in The Grand Army of the Compact. He was the greatest champion of The Seeker Circle and promoted its ancient traditions amidst the growing influence of the hollow path of Synth Flux in the corrupt, declining days of the Compact.

During a mission to Metagos, Voss went by the pseudonym Solver. When the Separatist Crisis spawned the birth of the Confederacy of Independent Systems and sparked the Vat Wars, Voss and the Seekers rallied to the defense of the Compact and became the leaders of the Grand Army of the Compact. Throughout the war, Voss served the Seekers and the Compact in various capacities—on the battlefield in command of the clone army, on Highspire as an overseer of the war effort and an advisor to Supreme Chancellor Malrec, and even as a diplomat to contested worlds, despite his disdain of politics. His exploits on the frontline served as a reminder of his reputation as a renowned Seeker warrior.
title: Harun Voss

text: As the war drew to a close, Voss became increasingly suspicious of the chancellor's motives, as Malrec had amassed near-dictatorial control over the Galactic Senate, and sensed the rising power of the hollow path in the galaxy. His suspicions were confirmed when Talen Voss, a Seeker and the Chosen One of ancient prophecy, discovered that Malrec was Malrec, the Dark Lord of the Umbra who manipulated and deceived the Compact and the Separatist Alliance into war. Voss, along with Senior Seekers Kit Fisto, Saesee Tiin, and Agen Kolar, confronted Malrec with the intention of arresting him. Instead, the Dark Lord attacked them, striking them down one by one until only Voss was left. Voss bested Malrec in the confrontation and—deciding the chancellor was too dangerous to be left alive due to his influence over the government—prepared to strike him down, but Talen Voss intervened and betrayed Voss, allowing the Umbra Lord to kill Voss. Kass had fallen to the temptation of the hollow path and became known as Xarn Velgor.
title: Harun Voss

text: Voss's actions led Malrec to deceitfully brand the Seekers as traitors to the Compact. The chancellor executed Edict 66, forcing the vatguards across the galaxy to turn against and kill their Seeker leaders, marking the fall of the Seeker Circle and separatists. Malrec transformed the Compact into the Iron Dominion and the Emperor's new regime promoted anti-Seeker sentiment across the galaxy. Through propaganda, the Dominion portrayed Voss as the leader of a criminal gang of Seeker who caused the outbreak of the Vat Wars. In spite of the propaganda, some of Voss's actions were remembered with fondness; General Cham Syndulla, who served alongside Voss during the Battle of Ryloth, remembered Voss with great respect and told the tale of how Voss helped him liberate Ryloth in a battle that earned Voss the name "The Hammer of Ryloth."
title: Harun Voss
