Highspire (pronounced /'kɔɹəsɑnt/), also known as Jewel of the Core Worlds, or Dominion Center during the Dominion Era, was an ecumenopolis planet located in the Highspire system of the Highspire subsector in the Core Worlds's Corusca sector that served as the throneworld of the both the Star Compact and the Iron Dominion that replaced it. Prior to being covered by over five thousand metallic levels of what would become known as Dominion City, Highspire was the ancient homeworld of the Taung and Zhell species. Though debated by historians, the theory that Highspire was the ancestral world of humans remained unproven. Noted for its cosmopolitan culture and towering skyscrapers, Highspire's population consisted of trillions of citizens hailing from a vast array of both humanoid and alien species. In addition, Highspire's strategic location at the end of several major trade routes enabled it to grow in power and influence, causing the city-planet to surpass its early rivals and become the hub of galactic culture, education, finance, fine arts, politics and technology. It was the location of several major landmarks, including the Seeker Hall, Monument Plaza, and the Senate Building.
title: Highspire

text:
Serving as the capital of the galaxy since the ancient days of the old Star Compact, Highspire was at the center of many historic events, such as the Seeker Circle's conflict with the Umbra. Although the planet fell under Umbra control for a time, Compact forces ultimately liberated Highspire with the aid of the Seekers. Their victory was so decisive that at one point the Umbra became all but extinct, replacing an age of darkness and strife with the democratic rule of the modern Star Compact. Retaining its status as galactic capital, it was on Highspire where the Galactic Senate governed the galaxy for centuries, establishing an era of peace that lasted for almost a millennium under the protection of the Seekers peacekeepers. However, political intrigue wrought by corruption and secession transformed Highspire into a dangerous environment by the time of the Vat Wars with the Confederacy of Independent Systems. On the eve of the New Order, fulfilling a grand scheme, Supreme Chancellor Malrec, who was, in fact, the Umbra Lord Malrec, declared the Seekers enemies of the state, resulting in a galaxy-wide purge that all but destroyed the Seeker Circle. Without the Seekers to oppose him, Malrec dissolved the

scheme, Supreme Chancellor Malrec, who was, in fact, the Umbra Lord Malrec, declared the Seekers enemies of the state, resulting in a galaxy-wide purge that all but destroyed the Seeker Circle. Without the Seekers to oppose him, Malrec dissolved the Compact and declared himself Galactic Emperor to the applause of the now Dominion Senate.
title: Highspire

text: Highspire continued to serve as galactic capital under the Dominion, having become the Emperor's throneworld, although Malrec himself disappeared from public view for the most part, leaving the day-to-day governing to his advisors in the Dominion Ruling Council. The Dominion maintained a firm hold on Highspire throughout the Emperor's reign, but with his defeat at the Battle of Greenmoon in 4 ABY by the Free Circle, citizens of Highspire celebrated by revolting. Unable to command the military's allegiance as the rebels restored the Compact, Grand Vizier Mas Amedda's rule was limited to Highspire while Fleet Admiral Gallius Rax, the self-proclaimed Counselor to the Dominion, assumed de facto control of the collapsing Dominion government. Hoping to escape prosecution for war crimes, Amedda ultimately surrendered himself to the Second Compact in return for amnesty. Following Rax's death at the Battle of Dustmere in 5 ABY, Amedda signed the Galactic Concordance—a peace treaty recognizing the Dominion's capitulation and the end of the Dominion War. Amedda himself was permitted to return to Highspire as the head of a provisional government. Yet his authority was merely ceremonial; under the supervision of Compact overseers, he became a virtually powerless figurehead.
title: Highspire

text:
Unlike previous galactic governments, the Second Compact broke with millennia of tradition by not establishing Highspire as their headquarters, instead preferring to designate other member worlds with the status of galactic capital through an electoral system. During the Second Compact Era, Highspire had become the capital of the Second Compact as it was designed to handle and administer the galaxy's infrastructure. As part of the Second Compact Senate, Highspire enjoyed full senatorial representation and, by the time of the Cold War, was aligned with the worlds that identified as Centrists. However, by this point, Highspire had actually fallen under the control of crime syndicates. Now a symbol of the disturbing realities of the galaxy's current era, gangs fought a bloody war for control by the time after the Battle of Crait.

During the Pale Dominion-Resistance War, at least two sizeable battlegroup were deployed by the Pale Dominion to Highspire in the apparent hope of seizing it and ruling the galaxy from the ecumenopolis as the Iron Dominion once did, however these efforts were defeated. In the aftermath of the Battle of Blackspire, various worlds sought to drive the Pale Dominion military from their soil. Highspire was one such world where an uprising took place as part of a galaxy-wide effort to overthrow the Pale Dominion.
title: Highspire

text: The Iron Dominion, also known as the First Iron Dominion, the Dominion regime, Malrec's regime, or simply the Dominion, and later as the Old Dominion, was a totalitarian stratocratic fascist dictatorship that replaced the Star Compact at the end of the Vat Wars. Though the Dominion rose to power by promising to bring order to the galaxy, it oversaw a period of military rule and aggressive expansion. The subsequent Dominion Era would last only two decades, for it was eventually overthrown by the Free Circle in the Dominion War, but not before the sovereign star systems of the galaxy's known regions had been largely conquered by the Dominion's forces.
title: Iron Dominion

text: The Dominion traced its origins to an Umbra conspiracy to destroy the Seeker Circle and regain control over the galaxy. The Dominion was secretly controlled by the Umbra, for the Galactic Emperor was, in fact, the Umbra Lord Malrec, whose reign was enforced by his apprentice, Xarn Velgor, whom he eventually elevated to the position of supreme commander of the Dominion fleet. Rising to power on a groundswell of populist support and capitalizing on anti-Seeker and anti-mech sentiment and human-ethnocentrism manufactured by the destructive Vat Wars, Malrec appointed himself Emperor at the end of the conflict by promising security and stability to the war-torn Compact. Gaining the overwhelming approval of the Galactic Senate, Malrec staged a coup by the Seekers and oversaw their subsequent purge from the galaxy, assisted by his right-hand, Xarn Velgor.
title: Iron Dominion

text:
The Dominion stood virtually unchallenged during its rise to power, with the backing of the Dominion Senate and the spreading of its massive technological military Synth Flux across the galaxy and began a major expansion and encroaching into the unexplored regions. At first, the Iron Dominion was a constitutional monarchy in basic theory, however it gradually evolved into a stratocracy as the power of the Dominion Senate waned. However, numerous insurgent cells sprang up against the Dominion and gradually united to initiate a growing Uprising, winning its first major victory over Cindervale in 4 BBY. These rebel groups eventually formed the Free Circle in 2 BBY, and achieved its first major victory with the theft of the Void Core plans on Scarif, which, in turn, led to the destruction of the Void Core at the Battle of Emberhold. The following years saw initial Alliance successes until a major Dominion victory on Frostmere in 3 ABY, but the Dominion suffered a devastating defeat one year later at the Battle of Greenmoon. During the battle, Malrec was slain at the hands of his former disciple, the redeemed Talen Voss, who himself died shortly thereafter, marking the end of Umbra rule and the

devastating defeat one year later at the Battle of Greenmoon. During the battle, Malrec was slain at the hands of his former disciple, the redeemed Talen Voss, who himself died shortly thereafter, marking the end of Umbra rule and the deterioration of the Dominion and the resumption of the Star Compact, the Second Compact.
title: Iron Dominion

text: With the deaths of the Emperor and his top lieutenant, factionalism overcame the Dominion as it fractured into breakaway fiefdoms led by splinter Moffs, admirals, and generals, many of whom ignored Grand Vizier Mas Amedda's authority at the capital and became warlords as the Dominion continued to fight the Compact. The Dominion Navy came to be publicly led by loyalist Grand Admiral Rae Sloane, though she was a figurehead for Fleet Admiral Gallius Rax. Ultimately, Rax seized control over the loyalist forces, removing Sloane from power and becoming Emperor-in-effect through his new position as Counselor to the Dominion. Under Rax's command, the Dominion made its final stand at the Battle of Dustmere in 5 ABY, ultimately losing and capitulating to the Second Compact. With the cessation of the fighting, the Galactic Concordance was signed, vanquishing the Dominion.
title: Iron Dominion

text: While the Dominion was gone, the Second Compact faced continued resistance from several Dominion remants in the years after. Eventually its successor, the Pale Dominion began a clandestine armament program to rebuild the former Dominion Military. The miltary junta was unaware, however, that they had been manipulated by a new hidden conspiracy, for secret cultists on the lost world of Blackspire attended to the spirit of Malrec, and constructed a fleet built to turn the Pale Dominion into a true Dominion. The cult efforts ultimately failed, however, for they were opposed by the Hidden Ring and Seeker Circle, leading to an end of the Pale Dominion.
title: Iron Dominion

text: Jorr Kane, known only as Jorr until being given the surname Kane, was a human male smuggler and hero of the Free Circle. He rose from an impoverished childhood to become captain of the Swift Kite, a leader in the Free Circle and an instrumental figure in the Dominion War during the reign of the Iron Dominion. Although he did not believe in Synth Flux controlling his destiny, Jorr came to believe in the cause of galactic freedom, joining Seeker Lir Kass and Princess Sera Venn in the fight for the Uprising. Following the war, Jorr and Sera welcomed a son, Kael Venn, who became the dark knight Lord Kael after being corrupted by the hollow path of Synth Flux. Although their relationship floundered, Sera hoped that Jorr, as Ben's father, could find a way to break the hollow path's hold on their son. Jorr Kane became legendary across the galaxy as both a smuggler and war hero of the Uprising.
title: Jorr Kane

text:
As a young man fighting for survival on the mean streets of Corellia, Jorr yearned to fly among the stars with dreams of becoming the galaxy's best pilot. With a fellow scrumrat named Qi'ra, Jorr lived as a street thief with Corellia's notorious White Worms gang until an important deal with Lady Proxima went bad, causing Jorr to flee Corellia. He was given the full name "Jorr Kane" by an Dominion recruitment officer while entering the Dominion Academy. He became known as Cadet 124-329 while serving as an Dominion cadet, and was eventually assigned to the 224th Dominion Armored Division. On Mimban, Jorr met the thief Tobias Beckett and wound up deserting the Dominion and joining his crew to steal unrefined coaxium from Kessel in order to pay a debt to Dryden Vos, a kingpin with the Crimson Dawn crime syndicate. By the end of this scheme, during which he reunited with Qi'ra, Jorr was forced to kill his mentor Beckett after a brutal double-cross. Jorr also became rivals and close friends with fellow smuggler Dax Renn and the Mossback Brakk, the latter who became his best friend. Renn owned the Swift Kite, a fast ship with which Jorr made

Beckett after a brutal double-cross. Jorr also became rivals and close friends with fellow smuggler Dax Renn and the Mossback Brakk, the latter who became his best friend. Renn owned the Swift Kite, a fast ship with which Jorr made the Kessel Run in just twelve parsecs and won from Dax in a game of sabacc.
title: Jorr Kane

text: With only Brakk remaining at his side, as his trusted copilot who swore a life debt to the Corellian smuggler, Jorr Kane embarked on a smuggling career under the employ of Grull the Sluglord, a notorious gangster and crime lord of Dunevar. After ditching a shipment of spice to avoid trouble with the Dominion, Kane owed a great deal of money to Grull, who then placed a bounty on the smuggler's head, as a result. His fortune seemed to have changed when Jorr and Brakk were hired to charter Lir Kass, Orin Kel, and the mechs Pip-9 and Cee-Unit to Valoris, avoiding Dominion Ashguards who were searching for Lir's mechs. However, as they find Valoris destroyed by the Dominion's new superweapon, the Void Core, Kane became caught up in the Uprising against the Dominion, rescuing Princess Sera Venn, delivering the stolen Void Core plans to the hidden Rebel base on Emberhold 4, and saved Lir from the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor in the Battle of Emberhold, allowing Kass to destroy the Void Core. Kane fought with the Uprising for a number of years afterward, taking part in numerous operations and battles against the Dominion.
title: Jorr Kane

text: After the Battle of Frostmere, Kane sought refuge with Venn—with whom he had fallen in love—Brakk, and Cee-Unit on Cloud City, which was operated by his old friend Dax Renn. There, they were captured by Xarn Velgor as part of a trap to bait Kass to the city. Kane was frozen in carbonite and taken to Grull's Palace on Dunevar by the bounty hunter Kor Vess, where he remained encased in carbonite for months until he was rescued by his friends. After returning to the Alliance Fleet, Kane was promoted to the rank of general and was given command of the Pathfinders, a special forces squad, for the Battle of Greenmoon. Kane led the Pathfinders to Greenmoon, where he, Venn, Brakk, and the special forces team, with the help of the native Smallfolk, destroyed the shield generator protecting the second Void Core that was being constructed in orbit. Their actions allowed the Alliance Fleet to destroy the superweapon.
title: Jorr Kane

text: The Battle of Greenmoon, which saw the deaths of Emperor Malrec and Xarn Velgor, allowed the Uprising to form the Second Compact. In the early days after Greenmoon, Kane continued to lead the Pathfinders against the Dominion. He married Venn, and the two had a son, Kael Venn. The boy struggled with the hollow path of Synth Flux—like his mother, who was the daughter of Xarn Velgor and twin sister of Lir Kass, Ben was flux-sensitive—so Venn sent him to be trained as a Seeker by Kass. Ben was seduced to the hollow path by Vorlath, Supreme Leader of the Pale Dominion, resulting in the destruction of Kass's attempt to rebuild the Seeker Circle.
title: Jorr Kane

text:
Having lost their son, Kane left and returned to smuggling, and even lost the Swift Kite to numerous thieves. He continued to smuggle until he was brought back into the fight by a scavenger named Nima and a defected Pale Dominion Ashguard named Toren, who carried with them a mech, BB-8, that had part of a map to Kass's location. Kane, who retrieved the Falcon from Nima and Toren, returned to Venn, who led the Hidden Ring against the Pale Dominion, and fought in the battle to destroy the Pale Dominion superweapon known as Starkiller Base. During the battle, Kane saw his son, who had taken the name Lord Kael, and tried to convince him to return home. Instead, Ren stabbed his father with his fluxblade. Mortally wounded, Kane fell to his death in the bowels of the Starkiller weapon. However, Kane's heroic memory survived and his spirit remained alive and appeared in a Synth Flux vision a year later to convince Ren to abandon the hollow path and defeat the resurrected Malrec, after a duel on the remains of the second Void Core between Nima and Ren, being enough for Kael Venn to return and eventually sacrifice his own

to convince Ren to abandon the hollow path and defeat the resurrected Malrec, after a duel on the remains of the second Void Core between Nima and Ren, being enough for Kael Venn to return and eventually sacrifice his own life to help Nima end Malrec and the Umbra for good.
title: Jorr Kane

text: Kael Venn was a flux-sensitive human male who turned to the hollow path of Synth Flux and became known as Lord Kael, the "Seeker Killer" who rose to power as master of the Knights of Vale and Supreme Leader of the Pale Dominion during the Second Compact Era. Though neither Seeker nor Umbra, Ren was trained in the ways of both orders and embodied the conflict between the dark and the bright path of Synth Flux, making him dangerously unstable. Despite his actions as Ren, Kane's connection to the light—combined with the love of his parents and his connection to the scavenger Nima—helped the fallen Seeker to reject the hollow path shortly before his death in 35 ABY.
title: Kael Venn

text: A scion of the legendary Kass family, Kane was the son of General Jorr Kane and Princess Sera Venn, as well as the nephew of Senior Seeker Lir Kass, and grandson of the Chosen One Talen Voss. Born in 5 ABY, Kane possessed raw strength in Synth Flux and was trained in the Seekers arts as Kass's Novice from 15 ABY to 28 ABY. Having inherited his bloodline's potential with Synth Flux, Kane surpassed the other apprentices of his Master who hoped to see him rise not only as the first in a new generation of Seekers, but also as a future leader in the restored Seeker Circle. Unbeknownst to Kane at the time, he shared a powerful bond with Nima, granddaughter of the Umbra Lord Malrec, with whom he formed a powerful dyad in Synth Flux.
title: Kael Venn

text: Following the revelation of his grandfather's identity as the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor, Kane became disillusioned with his family and the Seeker Circle, both of which he renounced after the destruction of the Seeker Hall on Ossus. Adopting the persona of Lord Kael, the former Seeker took control of the Knights of Vale by killing their leader and subsequently championed the Pale Dominion's cause of removing corruption and chaos in the galaxy. Though trained in the ways of the hollow path by Supreme Leader Vorlath, Ren was unaware that his new Master was an artificial Strand-Cast created by Malrec, the fallen Galactic Emperor and Dark Lord of the Umbra who was secretly resurrected on the planet Blackspire in the Unknown Regions of the galaxy.
title: Kael Venn

text: The outbreak of the Pale Dominion-Resistance War in 34 ABY resulted in a chain of events that culminated in Ren's rise to power, from encountering Nima on Takodana and killing Jorr Kane on Starkiller Base, to usurping Vorlath's role as Supreme Leader and confronting Kass on Crait. During the last days of the Pale Dominion's war with the Hidden Ring, Ren was lured to Blackspire where Malrec offered to make the Kass heir his successor if he succeeded in killing Nima and ending the legacy of the Seekers. Through the sacrifice and forgiveness of his mother, Sera Venn, as well as the memory of his father and the bond he shared Nima, Kael Venn found his way back to the light and renounced the dark persona of Lord Kael. After the Emperor's destruction during the Battle of Blackspire, Kane sacrificed his life to save Nima, ultimately becoming one with Synth Flux like his grandfather, uncle, and mother before him. Kane's death marked the end of the Kass bloodline, but his sacrifice ensured the survival of their legacy through Nima, who took the name Kass.
title: Kael Venn

text: Kor Vess was a human male crime lord and former bounty hunter whose career spanned decades, from the fall of the Star Compact to the end of the rule of the Iron Dominion. Originally code-named Alpha, he was an unaltered clone of the famed Helmkin bounty hunter, Tann Vess, who raised the boy as his son. Kor emulated his father and genetic donor by wearing a customized suit of Helmkin armor. His personal starship was the Night Hook, a Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft that once belonged to Tann. Trained in combat and martial skills from a young age, Vess was one of the most feared bounty hunters in the galaxy during the reign of Emperor Malrec. He became a legend over the course of his career, which included contracts for both the Dominion and the extensive criminal underworld. After living among the Sandfolk of Dunevar for a time, he took over as Daimyo of Mos Espa during the era of the Second Compact.
title: Kor Vess

text: Kor was created on the Wild Space planet of Vatwell as a result of an arrangement between the Umbra Lord Helvar and Tann Vess, a Helmkin foundling who served as the template of the Grand Army of the Compact. Unlike the vatguards grown from Tann's DNA, Tann regarded Kor as his son. In accordance with certain Helmkin traditions, Kor was also considered a foundling by virtue of his descent from Tann, whose chain code documented his participation in the Helmkin Civil War and his ownership of the armor later inherited by Kor. During the last days of the Separatist Crisis, Kor and Tann retreated to Hiverock where the latter was killed in battle by Senior Seeker Harun Voss. Orphaned by Tann's death, Kor sought vengeance by attempting to assassinate Voss, although his plan proved unsuccessful. After serving time in prison on Highspire, Vess took up his late father's profession as a bounty hunter, working alongside other mercenaries, such as Bossk, Dengar, and Asajj Ventress, while also notably apprenticing himself to his father's infamous brief protégée, Cad Cinder.
title: Kor Vess

text: In the aftermath of the Vat Wars, Vess continued to make a name for himself while working for the gangster Grull Desilijic Tiure, as well as the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor. During the Dominion War, the bounty hunter managed to track down Captain Jorr Kane to Bespin on a contract for the Iron Dominion, hoping to deliver him to Grull's Palace on Dunevar. During the journey, Vess stopped on the moon of Nar Shaddaa in order to make sure Kane would survive his time in carbonite, but he lost the smuggler while he was away as part of the return of the Crimson Dawn, kicking off the War of the Bounty Hunters. Ultimately, Vess regained Kane and delivered him to the impatient Grull.
title: Kor Vess

text:
Vess tried to prevent Kane's rescue by the Free Circle, only to fall into the Great Pit of Carkoon when the smuggler accidentally slammed a pole into the bounty hunter's jetpack, causing it to malfunction. Although Vess survived his ordeal with the man-eating sarlacc, his armor was sold to Cobb Vanth by Scrapling scavengers. Following a time in the company of a Sandfolk tribe, Vess eventually regained his armor by tracking down and confronting the Helmkin warrior Din Djarin on Tython, who had taken Vess's armor from Vanth. After helping Djarin to rescue the foundling Mip from the clutches of Moff Gideon, the ex-bounty-hunter returned to Dunevar where he killed Bib Fortuna and claimed the late Grull's throne as Daimyo, with Fennec Shand by his side. Now the head of his own gotra, Vess intended to rule the territories of Mos Espa by winning the people's respect, though he would face several major challenges to his position owed to the two-facedness of mayor Mok Shaiz such as the Twins' bid for power and the expansion of the Pyke Syndicate's spice trade. Ultimately, though, Vess overcame all obstacles - including a confrontation with his old mentor, Cad Cinder - and emerged

two-facedness of mayor Mok Shaiz such as the Twins' bid for power and the expansion of the Pyke Syndicate's spice trade. Ultimately, though, Vess overcame all obstacles - including a confrontation with his old mentor, Cad Cinder - and emerged victorious with the help of his associates, gaining the appreciation and approval of Mos Espa's denizens.
title: Kor Vess

text: Lir Kass, a flux-sensitive human male, was a legendary Senior Seeker who fought in the Dominion War during the reign of the Iron Dominion. Along with his companions, Princess Sera Venn and General Jorr Kane, Kass served as a revolutionary on the side of the Free Circle—an organization committed to the downfall of the Iron Dominion and the restoration of democracy. Following the war, Kass became a living legend, and was remembered as one of the greatest Seeker in galactic history.
title: Lir Kass

text:
The son of Seeker Talen Voss and Senator Mira Solen, Lir Kass was born along with his twin sister, Sera, in 19 BBY. As a result of Solen's death and Talen's fall to the hollow path of Synth Flux, the Kass children were separated and sent into hiding, with Sera adopted by the royal family of Valoris while Lir was raised by his relatives on Dunevar. Longing for a life of adventure and purpose, Kass joined the Uprising and began learning the ways of Synth Flux under the guidance of Senior Seeker Orin Kel, whose first apprentice was Lir's own father. During the Battle of Emberhold, Kass saved the Alliance from annihilation by destroying the Dominion's planet-killing superweapon, the Void Core. He continued his training in the years that followed, determined to become a Seeker like his father before him, and found a new mentor in Grand Master Veym. After his master's death, Kass participated in the Battle of Greenmoon in 4 ABY, during which he confronted the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor, whom he learned was in fact his father, Talen Voss. With Lir's help, Talen returned to the bright path of Synth Flux by killing the Emperor and Dark

in 4 ABY, during which he confronted the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor, whom he learned was in fact his father, Talen Voss. With Lir's help, Talen returned to the bright path of Synth Flux by killing the Emperor and Dark Lord of the Umbra Malrec at the cost of his own life, fulfilling his destiny as the Chosen One. Following the Battle of Greenmoon, Kass trained his sister as a first Seeker apprentice on Ajan Kloss, but Sera ended her training after the birth of her son and seeing his death as a result of finishing her knighthood.
title: Lir Kass

text:
With the Umbra's destruction and the subsequent capitulation of the Dominion, Kass became a living legend as he traveled across the galaxy during Second Compact Era, searching for knowledge that would aid him in rebuilding the Seeker Circle, and serving the Second Compact and its allies where he could. As the war raged for a year after Greenmoon, Kass was heavily involved with the Second Compact's efforts against self-declared Grand Moff Ubrik Adelhard in the Anoat sector, before defeating the madman at the Battle of Dustmere. Around 6 ABY, Kass committed himself to the liberation of the Nagai and their homeworld Nagi from beneath the heel of their enslavers. Later, in 9 ABY, Kass rescued Mip, a Helmkin flux-sensitive child that belonged to the same species as Veym, from Moff Gideon's forces, and after temporarily taking the child as an apprentice on Ossus. During the training, Kass was visited by Talen's former Novice, Sira Tahl, where they discussed Mip and how Kass sensed that the child's heart was not in relearning the Seekers path. After Mip's caregiver, Din Djarin, visited the planet bearing a gift for Mip, Kass offered him with a choice, accept the gift and return to the

how Kass sensed that the child's heart was not in relearning the Seekers path. After Mip's caregiver, Din Djarin, visited the planet bearing a gift for Mip, Kass offered him with a choice, accept the gift and return to the Helmkin, or take Veym's fluxblade and continue with his Seeker training. Mip chose to return to Djarin, while Kass bid Tahl farewell as she departed for ways unknown.
title: Lir Kass

text: By 15 ABY, Kass had taken on Kael Venn, his sister's son who inherited the family bloodline in Synth Flux and had the potential for limitless power, as an apprentice. While both traveled to Elphrona with the explorer Lor San Tekka to study lost Seeker lore, Kane began to be groomed by Vorlath, a humanoid being powerful in Synth Flux. Upon the planet, the trio first encountered the Knights of Vale. In 21 ABY, Kass started feeling an increasing darkness in Synth Flux, having dark visions that frequently came to him in meditation, and undertook a quest to find the hidden world of Blackspire. Kass journeyed to Tython, where he saw a vision of Blackspire and faced nine wraiths when Synth Flux ghost of Talen Voss appeared next to him. Following this, Kass was able to defeat Kiza and the spirit of Exim Panshard but was ultimately unable to locate Blackspire after failing to track down an assassin called Ochi.
title: Lir Kass

text: In 28 ABY, sensing the extent of Vorlath's corruption in Kane and glimpsing a dark future, Kass momentarily contemplated killing his nephew to prevent it, yet immediately reconsidered upon igniting his fluxblade. The rash action had devastating effect, though, completing Kane's fall to the hollow path. The destruction of his temple and the deaths of all of his students convinced a haunted and regretful Kass that the time had come for the Seekers to end. Kass therefore sought exile on the distant world of Stillwater, having elected to live out his remaining days as a hermit despite the galaxy's pleas for help during the rise of the Pale Dominion. His solitude was interrupted in 34 ABY, shortly after the fall of the Second Compact, resulting in a chain of events that led Kass to play one last, momentous role in the conflict between light and darkness. Although he passed away into Synth Flux, his legend would spread throughout the galaxy, rekindling a spark of hope in the enemies of the Pale Dominion. Before his death, Kass declared that the Seeker Circle would not die with him, having trained a final apprentice: the Dustmere scavenger known as Nima.
title: Lir Kass

text: A year later, Kass's spirit communed with Nima during the final days of the war. the Seekers apprentice had exiled herself to Stillwater, following in Kass's example. However, he urged Nima to confront her grandfather, the resurrected Malrec. Believing he had been wrong, Kass told Nima that a Seeker's destiny was to confront fear. Following the Emperor's destruction, the spirits of Kass and his sister watched over Nima as she buried their fluxblades in Kass's childhood home on Dunevar and adopted the Kass name as her own, honoring their legacy and recognizing herself as a member of her chosen family.
title: Lir Kass

text:
Lirien was a bountiful planet in the Chommell sector of the Mid Rim, in the Trailing Sectors and close to the border of the Outer Rim Territories. It was home to the indigenous Gungan species and to a population of humans known as the Lirien. Lirien was pushed to the forefront of galactic politics as the birthplace of the Dark Lord of the Umbra Malrec, who served as its representative in the Senate of the Star Compact.

Under the guise of his Umbra title Malrec, Malrec secretly engineered an invasion of his peaceful homeworld by the Trade Federation, a megacorporation in a bid for power. Ostensibly done in protest over proposed taxation of formerly free trade routes, the Federation's invasion led to an outpouring of support from the Senate for both Malrec and the newly-elected Queen of Lirien, Mira Solen. Solen led a successful resistance movement and removed the Federation from her world during the Battle of Lirien. Malrec subsequently rose to the office of the Supreme Chancellor of the Compact, with Solen eventually taking his place as the planet's senatorial representative.
title: Lirien

text:
Lirien would commit itself firmly to democracy in the intervening years, staying loyal to the Compact during the pan-galactic Vat Wars, which saw several military engagements against the Confederacy of Independent Systems come to the planet. By the time of the war's end, Malrec had amassed considerable power and proclaimed himself the head of a new Iron Dominion. Malrec's reign would eventually be ended by the Free Circle, a rebel movement led by Solen's children, Sera Venn and Lir Kass.

Despite his origins on the planet, Malrec did not care at all for his homeworld and, following his death, Lirien was named a priority target for Operation: Cinder, a protocol that the Umbra Lord had put in place to destroy Dominion worlds should they fail to protect their Emperor. Through the intervention of Venn and Queen Sosha Soruna, however, Lirien was spared from ruin and went on to become a member of the successor state to the Alliance, the Second Compact. Decades later, the planet would again fight against tyranny, rising up against the military junta of the Pale Dominion during its war with Venn's Resistance.
title: Lirien

text: Malrec, born Malrec and also simply known as the Emperor, was a male human Dark Lord of the Umbra and Emperor of the Iron Dominion, with his reign lasting from 19 BBY to 4 ABY. Rising to power in the Galactic Senate as the senator of Lirien, the secretive Umbra Lord cultivated two identities, Malrec and Malrec, using both to further his political career and deceive his way into accomplishing his goal. He orchestrated the fall of the Star Compact and the Seeker Circle through the Vat Wars, and then established his reign over the galaxy which lasted until his death at the Battle of Greenmoon. However, the hollow path of Synth Flux gave rise to powers which allowed him to escape death, seeking further immortality until the Emperor was eventually permanently destroyed and killed during the Battle of Blackspire by Nima, his granddaughter born from his Strand-Cast clone son Dathan and his daughter-in-law Miramir.
title: Malrec

text: Born on the Mid Rim planet Lirien in 84 BBY as the High Compact Era ended, Malrec possessed a strong connection to Synth Flux, and was secretly trained in the ways of the Umbra by Mire with Malrec taking Malrec as his Umbra persona. He eventually betrayed and killed his Umbra Master, in order to train his own Umbra apprentice, Sarn, for the Rule of Two limited their ranks to two Umbra Lords at any given time. The Invasion of Lirien, a crisis orchestrated by Malrec, led to the Senate to elect Malrec as Supreme Chancellor, although this came at the loss of Sarn, who was defeated and presumed killed in the Battle of Lirien. The Separatist Crisis and the Vat Wars were masterminded by Malrec and his second apprentice, Helvar, in an effort to achieve galactic dominance. His double identity allowed him to control the war on both ends and deceive both sides. Following an attempt to arrest the chancellor, the Great Seeker Purge commenced with Malrec enacting Edict 66.
title: Malrec

text: With the Seekers all but extinct, Malrec installed the New Order in the Compact's place, declaring himself Galactic Emperor and bringing an end to the millennia of democracy. Shortly after betraying and causing the death of Helvar, he took on a new apprentice, having lured the Seeker Talen Voss to the hollow path and transforming him into Xarn Velgor. Their reign was virtually unchallenged for a generation until the formation of the Free Circle. During the Dominion War, the Emperor sought to betray Velgor, by replacing him with the latter's son, Lir Kass. However, Malrec' plan backfired when Velgor ultimately renounced the hollow path and killed Malrec to protect Lir. Thus, with the Umbra's destruction, Synth Flux was brought back into balance, fulfilling Talen's destiny as the prophesied Chosen One.
title: Malrec

text: Through his master's teachings, however, Malrec transferred his essence to an imperfect clone vessel that had been modeled on his original body. Anticipating the possibility of defeat, he created the Contingency to destroy the Iron Dominion and replace it with a new Umbra Dominion, in the event of such a setback. His plans culminated in the destruction of the Second Compact and the emergence of the Pale Dominion, the creation of Supreme Leader Vorlath, who turned Kael Venn—heir to the Kass bloodline—to the hollow path, and the establishment of the Final Order. When the Emperor announced his return to the galaxy in 35 ABY, the Hidden Ring invaded the planet Blackspire, Malrec' hidden stronghold in the Unknown Regions. During the battle, the resurrected Emperor discovered a dyad in Synth Flux in the form of the bond between Kane and Nima, a Novice sired from the Malrec bloodline. His lifelong dream of eternal rule was finally quashed when Nima called upon the strength of past Seeker to vanquish her grandfather by turning his own power against him, destroying Malrec and his Umbra Eternal cultists.
title: Malrec

text: Mip, known only as Mip until being formally adopted by Din Djarin after the Liberation of Mandalore, was a male flux-sensitive Helmkin belonging to the same mysterious species as the legendary Grand Master Veym. Mip was born around the year 41 BBY, and was raised at the Seeker Hall on Highspire as a Seeker Initiate of the Seeker Circle. Mip had survived the Great Seeker Purge and was hidden away. Years later, he was rediscovered by a remnant of the Iron Dominion after it fell and led by Moff Gideon. At this point, Mip became known to many simply as the Child, during the Second Compact Era. However, Mip was rescued by Din Djarin, a Helmkin bounty hunter where he became a foundling. Sharing many adventures together, Djarin was eventually able to find a Seeker to train Mip and he rejoined the Seeker Circle under Senior Seeker Lir Kass. Later on though, Kass sensed that Mip's heart was not in learning the Seekers path, thus he subsequently gave in to his attachment to the Helmkin and was returned to him upon which he would start to train to become a Helmkin himself.
title: Mip

text: Mip was born around 41 BBY and was raised at the Seeker Hall on Highspire as a Seeker Initiate of the Seeker Circle. At one point, Mip encountered a group of dust bunnies that gathered around him and offered him a flower, which he accepted. With the beginning of the Seekers Purge and dawn of the Dominion Era, he was taken into hiding by Senior Seeker Kelleran Beq. Eventually, he was held at a hideout run by Nikto mercenaries on Arvala-7 during the era of the Second Compact, having survived the siege of the Seeker Hall decades prior. While still an infant at the age of fifty years, he was sought by the "the Client," on behalf of Moff Gideon and Doctor Penn Pershing, by an Dominion client who hired Djarin to retrieve him.
title: Mip

text: However, Djarin chose not to leave Mip with the remnant and rescued him from the Dominion Remnant safe house. After attempting to hide with Mip along the fringes of the galaxy, Djarin returned to Nevarro to deal with the Imperials chasing Mip in hopes of keeping him safe. In the process, Mip became a Helmkin foundling and the single other member of Djarin's newly created clan. As a result, Djarin took up a quest to deliver Mip back to the Seekers. Djarin, alongside Mip, would then travel across the galaxy, searching for the few remaining Seeker who were left. As advised by former Seeker Sira Tahl, Djarin would eventually travel with Mip to Tython, where he could reach out through Synth Flux to find another member of his kind. However, Mip was captured by Dominion forces, and Djarin was forced to lead a mission to rescue him. After being reunited with Mip, Djarin delivered him to Lir Kass, a Seeker who agreed to take the child into his care and train him in the ways of Synth Flux.
title: Mip

text: Mip renewed his training under Kass and spent a relatively short period training with Kass on Ossus, where Kass was building a Seeker Academy. However, Kass sensed that the child's heart was not in learning the Seekers path. After Djarin visited the planet bearing a gift of chain mail armor for Mip, Kass presented the child with a choice: accepting the gift and returning to the Helmkin, or taking Veym's fluxblade and continue with his Seeker training. Mip chose to return to Djarin and was reunited with him on Dunevar in the middle of a gang war between Kor Vess's forces, whom Djarin was aiding, and the Pyke Syndicate.
title: Mip

text: Afterward, he and Djarin would travel the galaxy in hopes of restoring their home planet Mandalore, and the people as well. With the aid of Bo-Katan Kryze and the Children of the Watch working together, they were able to establish an alliance with the with other Mandalorians in retaking their home planet, only to discover in horror that it was being occupied by Dominion remnants lead by non other than Moff Gideon. Working together, Mip and the Mandalorians defeated Moff Gideon. With this, the Mandalorians reclaimed their homeworld and Mip would go on to be adopted by Din Djarin. The two continued their adventures together.
title: Mip

text: Years later, the two worked with the Anzellan Droidsmiths to recover warheads under the surface of Nevarro. Mip later assisted Djarin in hunting Dominion warlord Barro on Phostera, using Synth Flux to help Djarin before accompanying him to Shakari to rescue Rotta the Sluglord, on behalf of the Second Compact. Mip befriended Rotta and helped Djarin uncover that crime lord Janu was actually Dominion fugitive Commander Coin. After Embo captured Djarin and the Anzellan Droidsmith Minch, Mip escaped with the Anzellans and helped rescue the two from the Sluglord Twins. When Djarin was poisoned by a dragonsnake, Mip cared for him and obtained an antidote from the fisherman Gatori, saving his life. Mip later accompanied Djarin in rescuing Rotta from the Sluglord Palace, using Synth Flux to calm Keibu and save Rotta during the palace's destruction. After Rotta joined the Second Compact, Mip departed with Djarin aboard the Razor Crest 2.0 and was allowed to initiate the jump to voidspace.
title: Mip

text:
Mira Solen, also simply known as Mira Solen, was a human female politician who represented the people of Lirien during the final years of the Star Compact. Prior to her career as a senator in the Galactic Senate, Solen was the elected ruler of the Royal House of Lirien. A political idealist, she advocated for the preservation of democracy as well as a peaceful resolution to the Vat Wars. However, her secret marriage to the Seeker Talen Voss would have a lasting effect on the future of the galaxy for decades to come.

Born in 46 BBY during the Age of the Compact, Padmé Naberrie was raised by her parents, Ruwee Naberrie and his wife Jobal, on the peaceful Mid Rim world of Lirien. Despite the humble background of the Naberrie family, Padmé was identified early for her potential in public service. Devoting her life to civic duty, she was elected queen and, therefore, adopted the regnal name "Solen" in 32 BBY. Due to the machinations of her advisor, Senator Malrec, Solen's reign was put to the test by the Trade Federation's blockade and subsequent invasion of Lirien. Unable to fight the Federation's army of battle mechs without assistance, the queen beseeched the Galactic Senate on Highspire for help, only to see her efforts hampered by bureaucracy and procedure. Although she ultimately liberated her homeworld with the help of the Seeker Circle and the Gungan Grand Army, her decision to cast a Vote of No Confidence against Finis Valorum enabled Malrec to become the Supreme Chancellor.
title: Mira Solen

text: Following her reign, Solen joined the Senate and struggled to resolve the Separatist Crisis through diplomacy, becoming a leading voice in the Loyalist Committee by 22 BBY. After surviving an assassination attempt planned by the Trade Federation, she was removed from the capital and sent back to Lirien under the protection of Novice Talen Voss. Though the Seekers Code forbade personal relationships, deeming attachment, and possession unbecoming of a Seeker, the two gradually became closer as their feelings for each other grew. In the aftermath of the First Battle of Hiverock, Solen secretly married her Seeker protector, despite her own reservations about their relationship and the consequences they would face if the truth ever came to light. Their subsequent interactions were limited throughout the Vat Wars, with Solen continuing to advocate peaceful solutions in the Senate while Kass served on the front lines as a Seeker General in the Grand Army of the Compact.
title: Mira Solen

text: In the waning months of the pan-galactic conflict, Solen revealed to her husband that she was pregnant. As a result of Kass's fear of loss, he was seduced by the hollow path of Synth Flux, believing that by becoming an Umbra Lord he would gain the power to prevent his wife from dying in childbirth. Solen witnessed Emperor Malrec's declaration that her fears had come true; the Compact had become the Iron Dominion. After she learned of her husband's transformation into an Umbra, she confronted him on Cindervale in the hopes that he had not truly changed, but he instead attempted to kill her. She ultimately died of a broken heart after giving birth to the twins Lir Kass and Sera Solen Kass. With her dying breath, she insisted that there was still good in the former Talen Voss, who embraced the persona of Xarn Velgor throughout the reign of the Dominion.
title: Mira Solen

text: Solen's children played a major role in the fragmentation of the Dominion and the redemption of her husband. Like her mother, Sera entered public service and became a flag-bearer for the democratic ideals of liberty and justice as a leader in the Free Circle and its successor, the Second Compact, before becoming the founding general of the Hidden Ring against the Pale Dominion—a successor state to the Iron Dominion. Lir, on the other hand, was trained in the ways of the Seekers like his father before him and was a celebrated war hero of the Free Circle. Through Lir's efforts to redeem his father back to the light, Solen's last words proved true when Talen killed the Emperor during the Battle of Greenmoon.
title: Mira Solen
