Mirewood was a remote, unexplored planet in the Mirewood system, and one of the purest places in the galaxy within Synth Flux. A remote world of swamps and forests, it served as a refuge for Seeker Grand Master Veym during his exile after the destruction of the Seeker Circle. Lir Kass received advanced training in the ways of Synth Flux under Senior Seeker Veym on Mirewood, and it was later the place of Veym's death and transformation into Synth Flux.
title: Mirewood

text: Mossreach, also known as Planet Mossback C to some humans in the Core Worlds, was a wroshyr tree-covered forest planet located in the southwestern quadrant of the galaxy and the homeworld of the Mossback species. Four millennia before the Battle of Emberhold, Mossreach was discovered by the Czerka Corporation, who enslaved the Mossback population and renamed the planet G5-623, later to Edean. Using superior technology, the company managed to enslave the Mossbacks until an uprising drove the oppressors away. During the Vat Wars, Mossreach was a member of the Star Compact, and endured enslavement under the Iron Dominion, the Compact's successor. Later, during the rise of the Second Compact, Mossreach was liberated with the help of Compact forces led by Jorr Kane.
title: Mossreach

text:
Needlewing Starfighters, otherwise referred to as the Needlewing class, were a type of starfighter marked by their distinctive S-foils that resembled the High Galactic script's character "X" in attack formation. They were heavily armed with four laser cannons on the S-foils and proton torpedo launchers in the fuselage. Needlewings were designed for dogfighting and long missions. During the Dominion War, the Free Circle used Needlewing models like the T-65B Needlewing and T-65C-A2 Needlewing in many battles, deploying Needlewings in engagements such as the Attack on Lothal, the Battle of Emberhold, the Battle of Greenmoon, and the Battle of Dustmere.

Approximately thirty years later, a different and upgraded variation of Needlewing, the T-70, was used by the Hidden Ring, whereas a more advanced model, the T-85, was used by the Second Compact Defense Fleet.
title: Needlewing

text: Nima Kass, also known simply as Nima, was a Seeker member of the Hidden Ring during the war against the Pale Dominion. The human woman was a scavenger on the planet Dustmere, but her life was changed by tumultuous events in the last days of the Second Compact Era. Nima's decision to help the mech BB-8 set her on a course to discovering Synth Flux awakening within her, leading her to seek out Senior Seeker Lir Kass for training. Despite her commitment to the Seeker Circle and the bright path of Synth Flux, Nima felt the pull to the hollow path due to her anger as well as the adversarial relationship she had with Kael Venn, a fallen Seeker who joined the Pale Dominion as a warrior named Lord Kael; they shared a unique bond as a dyad in Synth Flux.
title: Nima Kass

text:
Nima was born on Hyperkarn in 15 ABY during the rise of the Second Compact. Her father, Dathan, was a bioengineered Strand-Cast cloned from the genetic template of Malrec, the Umbra Lord who ruled the Iron Dominion as Emperor Malrec until his death and resurrection following the Battle of Greenmoon. The clone and his wife, Miramir, chose to live as simple junk traders in order to hide their daughter, who inherited Malrec' connection to Synth Flux, from his followers. Even after the deaths of her parents, Nima was unaware of her Malrec bloodline and was forced to survive on her own in the Dustmere desert, and became a skilled mechanic, pilot, and combatant in the process. Her isolated life was disrupted shortly before war broke out across the galaxy in 34 ABY between the Pale Dominion and the Hidden Ring. Determined to help the Hidden Ring, Nima gained several new allies including Toren, a renegade Ashguard, as well as the veterans Jorr Kane and Brakk aboard the Swift Kite. In the course of their journey, she discovered her latent Synth Flux powers and sought guidance under Lir Kass, who taught her the art of Synth Flux despite his decision to

veterans Jorr Kane and Brakk aboard the Swift Kite. In the course of their journey, she discovered her latent Synth Flux powers and sought guidance under Lir Kass, who taught her the art of Synth Flux despite his decision to end the Seekers legacy. After Kass sacrificed himself to save the Hidden Ring, Nima assumed his mantle as the last Seeker and became the apprentice of General Sera Venn.
title: Nima Kass

text: With the return of Malrec in 35 ABY, Nima set out to find the dark world of Blackspire and prevent the Umbra from being reborn through the resurrected Dark Lord. It was through Lord Kael that Nima discovered her origins as Malrec's granddaughter, and upon confronting the resurrected Emperor in person, she was nearly swayed to the hollow path of Synth Flux, thus falling into his trap of transferring his spirit into her, which will allow him to possess her body. However, Nima was saved by Kael Venn after he renounced his dark alter ego. Aided by the spirits of all the Seekers, Nima died vanquishing her grandfather, causing Kane to make the ultimate sacrifice in order to bring Nima back to life. The two embraced and shared a kiss as Kane peacefully vanished in Nima's arms. Although Kane was the last of the Kass bloodline, Nima assumed the name "Kass" to honor their memory and in recognition of her chosen family. Sometime later, the now self-proclaimed Nima Kass became a Senior Seeker.
title: Nima Kass

text:
Orin Kel was a legendary flux-sensitive human male Senior Seeker who served on the Seekers High Council during the final years of the Compact Era. As a High Seeker General, Kel served in the Grand Army of the Compact that fought against the Separatist mech Army during the Vat Wars, and was nicknamed "the Negotiator." Kel, however, was forced into exile as a result of the Great Seeker Purge initiated by the Compact's own vatguards when Compact Supreme Chancellor, secretly Malrec, implemented Edict 66. As a mentor, Kel was responsible for training two members of the Kass family, Talen and Lir Kass, both of whom served in turn as his Novice in the ways of Synth Flux.

Kel was born on the planet Stewjon in 57 BBY. He was flux-sensitive, and therefore taken from his family and inducted into the Seeker Circle as a child. Raised in the Seekers Grand Temple on the planet Highspire, Kel was assigned to Senior Seeker Quin Jor. In 32 BBY, Kel attained the rank of Seeker by defeating the Umbra Lord Sarn during the Invasion of Lirien. He also chose to train Talen Voss—the prophesied Chosen One who was destined to destroy the Umbra and restore balance to Synth Flux—having promised Jor who died in the fluxblade duel against Sarn.
title: Orin Kel

text: With the advent of the Vat Wars in 22 BBY, Kel adopted the military rank of High Seeker General in the Grand Army of the Star Compact, and was given command of the Open Circle Fleet, the Third Systems Army, and the 7th Sky Corps. Clone Marshal Commander Cody served as his second-in-command throughout the galaxy-wide conflict, with their forces achieving multiple victories over the Confederacy of Independent Systems. In the midst of the war, his old enemy Sarn re-emerged into galactic affairs, bent on revenge against Kel for his debilitating defeat decades prior. Though they clashed in heated duels on multiple occasions, Sarn failed to end Kel's life or cripple his spirit, despite murdering his former love, Satine Kryze, Duchess of Mandalore.
title: Orin Kel

text:
Ten years later, Kel left exile to rescue Sera Venn, Lir's twin sister, and was pursued by the Dominion's Inquisitorius and Velgor himself. Later, Kel was hunted down once again by Sarn, whom he finally slew to protect the young Lir. Kel began the boy's Seeker training in 1 BBY, and soon after encountered Velgor aboard the first Void Core, where he sacrificed himself to ensure that Lir and his allies escaped from the Umbra Lord. In death, Kel became one with Synth Flux which allowed him to continue guiding Lir throughout the Dominion War. In 4 ABY, Kel reunited with his former student, Talen Voss, who died destroying his Umbra Master in order to save his son. Kel was remembered as a legendary Senior Seeker during the rise of the Second Compact; Kael Venn, the son of Lir's twin sister, Princess Sera Venn, was named after Kel. Kane's turn to the hollow path left Lir disillusioned with the Seeker Circle's legacy, and he held Kel responsible for Talen's transformation into Velgor. However, Lir's faith would eventually be restored with the aid of Malrec's granddaughter Nima, to whom Kel would lend his voice and strength in a final battle and

Circle's legacy, and he held Kel responsible for Talen's transformation into Velgor. However, Lir's faith would eventually be restored with the aid of Malrec's granddaughter Nima, to whom Kel would lend his voice and strength in a final battle and victory against her resurrected ancestor on Blackspire in 35 ABY.
title: Orin Kel

text:
Pip-9, pronounced Pip-9 and often referred to as R2 (Pip), was an R2-series astromech mech manufactured by Industrial Automaton with masculine programming. A smart, spunky mech who served a multitude of leaders, Pip-9 was never given a full memory wipe nor did he ever receive new programming, with these factors resulting in an adventurous and independent attitude. Often finding himself in pivotal moments in galactic history, his bravery and ingenuity saved the galaxy on numerous occasions.

Beginning his service in the employ of Queen Solen of Lirien, Pip-9 wound up serving Seeker Talen Voss during the waning years of the Star Compact, often accompanied by the protocol mech Cee-Unit in many adventures throughout the Vat Wars. After Kass turned to the hollow path of Synth Flux, the mech served Senator Bail Venn for a time in the Dominion Senate. Around nineteen years following the purge of the Star Compact, Pip-9 played a pivotal role in helping the Free Circle destroy the Dominion's Void Core superweapon. He carried technical readouts vital to its destruction. Serving Seeker Lir Kass, the son of his two former masters throughout the Dominion War, he participated in both the Battles of Frostmere and Greenmoon, and witnessed the successful destruction of the Dominion's second Void Core four years after the first one was demolished.
title: Pip-9

text:
In the subsequent thirty years, R2 accompanied Lir Kass until the undoing of his attempted resurrection of the Seeker Circle in 28 ABY. Following Lir's disappearance, R2 entered a self-imposed low power mode as newer mech models started to out-compute the aging astromech. Despite this, his celebrated role in the Uprising protected him from the usual recycling procedure of many old mechs, allowing him a semi-retirement in the Hidden Ring as he pored over several decades of uninterrupted data, and "dreamed" of his greatest adventures.

Following his reawakening after the Battle of Starkiller Base, R2 went on to accompany the flux-sensitive scavenger Nima on her journey to train under Lir Kass on Stillwater, the planet of the First Seeker Hall, where the mech was reunited with his old master. Pip-9 continued to aid the Hidden Ring alongside his longtime counterpart Cee-Unit throughout the Pale Dominion-Resistance War, culminating in a decisive victory at the Battle of Blackspire, in which he was an active participant in the role of copilot for General Cass Drell.
title: Pip-9

text: Quin Jor, a flux-sensitive human male, was a venerable if maverick Senior Seeker who lived during the last years of the Compact Era. He was a wise and well-respected member of the Seeker Circle, and was offered a seat on the Seekers Council, but chose to reject and follow his own path. Adhering to a philosophy centered around the Living Synth Flux, Jor strove to follow the will of Synth Flux even when his actions conflicted with the wishes of the High Council. After encountering Talen Voss, Jor brought him to the Seeker Hall on Highspire, convinced he had found the Chosen One. His dying wish was for Kass to become a Seeker and ultimately restore balance to Synth Flux.
title: Quin Jor

text: Born on the Core World Highspire, the capital of the Star Compact around 80 BBY, Jor learned the ways of Synth Flux as the Novice of Senior Seeker Helvar before ultimately attaining the rank of Seeker in around 58 BBY. In 44 BBY he would go on to take an apprentice of his own, Orin Kel, who adhered to the principles of the Seekers Code more than his own master. Although their relationship was sometimes tough, the two Seeker overcame early difficulties during a mission to Pijal, which concluded in Jor turning down a request to join the Seekers Council to continue teaching his apprentice. When the Trade Federation initiated a blockade of the Mid Rim planet Lirien in 32 BBY, Jor and Kel were dispatched to resolve the crisis at the request of Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum. Influenced by the mysterious Umbra Lord Malrec, the Federation launched a full-scale invasion of Lirien, forcing the Seekers to rescue Queen Mira Solen after the fall of Theed.
title: Quin Jor

text: During their journey to the galactic capital, the group was forced to land on the Outer Rim planet Dunevar where Jor encountered a young slave named Talen Voss. Using a scientific method to gauge the boy's potential, he learned that Kass had more flux-marks in his blood than any flux-sensitive in galactic history, including Grand Master Veym. The revelation that he was the result of a miracle birth—a child born of a mother, but had no father—confirmed Jor's suspicion that Kass was the Chosen One destined to restore balance to Synth Flux. Before departing the desert world with Kass, Jor was confronted by Malrec' Umbra apprentice Sarn. Although their duel was brief, it convinced Jor that the Umbra had returned after a millennium of silence.
title: Quin Jor

text: At the Temple, Jor was adamant that Kass was the Chosen One and should, therefore, be inducted into the Seeker Circle. However, having inspected Kass for themselves, the High Council deemed him too old, emotional, and dangerously full of fear and anger. Jor saw their decision as a temporary setback, but the need to resolve the situation on Queen Solen's homeworld forced him to set aside his plans for Kass. During the Battle of Lirien, Jor and Kel confronted Sarn together. While they initially managed to fend off the Umbra Lord's attacks, master and apprentice were eventually separated during the fluxblade duel, resulting in Jor sustaining a mortal injury. Rushing to his master's aid, Kel fought and ultimately defeated the Dathomirian Umbra, but could not save Jor. With his last breath, Jor made Kel promise that he would take Kass as his apprentice. Having secured Kel's word, Jor became one with Synth Flux, dying with the certainty that he had found the prophesied Chosen One.
title: Quin Jor

text:
Sarn was a flux-sensitive Dathomirian Zabrak male who was apprenticed to the Umbra Lord Malrec, and after his defeat by the Seekers Orin Kel, he established himself as a crime lord during the Vat Wars and the Dominion Era. The renegade Umbra Lord was a formidable warrior, driven by hatred against the Seekers and his former Umbra Master.

Born in 54 BBY during the time of the Star Compact, Sarn was a son of Mother Talzin, who led the Nightsisters of Dathomir. Taken as a child by Malrec, Sarn was molded into a deadly Dark Lord of the Umbra, growing in hatred of the Seekers who served the Compact and the bright path of Synth Flux—while the Seeker Circle had deemed the Umbra extinct for a thousand years, Sarn's power-hungry master set his Grand Plan into motion with the Trade Federation's Invasion of Lirien in 32 BBY. Sarn announced the return of the Umbra on Dunevar, where he tried to kill the Seekers emissaries of the Compact's Supreme Chancellor. However, Sarn's failure to do so allowed Senior Seeker Quin Jor and his pupil, Novice Orin Kel, to bring Queen Solen of Lirien and a boy strong in Synth Flux—exceptionally so, to the extent that Jor believed this "Talen Voss" to be the prophesied Chosen One who would bring balance to the galaxy—to Highspire, the heart of the Compact.
title: Sarn

text: Nevertheless, Malrec used the resultant crisis in the Senate to elevate his public persona, Senator Malrec of Lirien, to the position of Supreme Chancellor. The Queen and Seeker, meanwhile, joined forces with the native Gungans on Lirien to throw off the yoke of the Trade Federation. Sarn, having been dispatched by his master to oversee the Federation leadership, was redirected to handle the Seekers. Sarn dealt a fatal blow to Quin Jor, but Kel in turn defeated Sarn by bisecting him at the waist, with the Dark Lord falling to the abyss and presumed dead. He was actually alive, sustained by his rage in the wastelands of Lotho Minor. Around the same time, Malrec took on Jor's Senior Seeker, Helvar, as his new apprentice. A decade afterward, Helvar set the second part of the Umbra plan into motion with the start of the Vat Wars.
title: Sarn

text: As the galaxy plunged into war, Mother Talzin plotted against Helvar and had one of her sons, Savage Opress, seek out Sarn. Indeed, the defeated Zabrak was brought back to Dathomir and had his sanity and mobility restored by Talzin's magick. Sarn trained his newfound brother in the ways of the Umbra, initially wanting to take revenge against Orin Kel. After the brothers were defeated by the Seekers, they took their chance to increase their powers with a brazen takeover of Mandalore, the erstwhile neutral world torn between the interests of the Compact and the Separatists. Sarn seized control of the self-styled Helm Watch and used them terrorise Mandalore while he expanded his criminal enterprise, known as the Shadow Collective—the Pyke Syndicate, Black Sun, and the Sluglord Clan were coerced to join forces under the underworld's new crime lord—until he caught the attention of Malrec, who killed Sarn's brother and captured Sarn.
title: Sarn

text: Sarn was rescued by his Helmkin loyalists and immediately tried to reconsolidate his Shadow Collective. However, he and his mother's desire for revenge against Malrec was checked by the Dark Lord, who instead decimated their homeworld of Dathomir with the use of the Separatists led by Helvar and General Vex. Mother Talzin herself was killed while protecting Sarn, and his syndicates were weakened. While he regathered with his loyalists on Mandalore, Sarn sensed that his former master's Grand Plan was coming to its climax and wished to lure Talen Voss—the Seeker trained by Orin Kel whom he correctly believed was central to Malrec' schemes—alongside Kel himself to Mandalore. Sarn's thirst for revenge was foiled again when Compact forces intervening on the side of the Mandalore resistance were instead led by Kass's old apprentice, Sira Tahl.
title: Sarn

text: While Sarn and Tahl fought at the Siege of Mandalore, Malrec successfully executed his plan to destroy the Seeker Circle and anoint himself Galactic Emperor. With the support of some Helmkin and Zabrak loyalists, Sarn continued trying to control the underworld but operated more clandestinely, away from the prying apparatus of the new Dominion regime. He was known in criminal circles as the Shadow Lord and was pursued by the Emperor's Inquisitors, who simply called him the Shadow. In the Dominion's later years, Sarn secretly coordinated the Five Crime Syndicates and controlled the Crimson Dawn syndicate through Dryden Vos and Qi'ra.
title: Sarn

text: Sarn also sought a great weapon on Malachor purported to be able of destroying all life and thus crossed paths with the Seekers Kanan Jarrus and Ezra Bridger as well as Sira Tahl. However, they were all stopped by Xarn Velgor, the fallen Kass. Sarn escaped and continued to tempt Bridger towards the hollow path in service of his own ends. Bridger rejected Sarn's overtures, but not before the former Umbra Lord used their connection to track his old nemesis Kel back to Dunevar. Their last duel ended with one fatal blow to Sarn. Learning that Kel had consigned himself to a life of exile to protect the prophesied Chosen One who would destroy the Umbra, Sarn died with the belief that he would ultimately be avenged.
title: Sarn

text:
The Seeker Circle, also known as the Order of the Seekers, and the New Seeker Circle under Senior Seeker Lir Kass, was a noble monastic and nontheistic religious order united in their devotion to the bright path of Synth Flux. They served as mediators, warriors, and with teaching and exploratory efforts. With a history dating back thousands of years before the rise of the Iron Dominion, the Seekers—noted for their fluxblades and natural ability to harness the powers of Synth Flux—stood as the guardians of peace and justice in the Star Compact. The Order was originally established on Stillwater in the Unknown Regions. In later years, the Seekers Grand Temple on the Core World Highspire served as the hub of all Seeker activity in the galaxy. The Temple was also a training school for younglings and Novices, who learned the ways of Synth Flux under the supervision of Senior Seekers, twelve of whom were elected to serve on the Seekers High Council—the Order's highest governing authority. The High Council's staff officers were the Grand Master, who functioned as the leader of the Order and was a title reserved for the wisest Senior Seeker, and the Master of the Order, who

High Council—the Order's highest governing authority. The High Council's staff officers were the Grand Master, who functioned as the leader of the Order and was a title reserved for the wisest Senior Seeker, and the Master of the Order, who served as the Council's appointed leader. the Seekers Code governed the Order's way of life; therefore, every Seeker was duty-bound to observe and uphold the Code or else risk expulsion from the Order.
title: Seeker Circle

text: The emergence of the Umbra Order was the result of a schism that fractured Seeker unity, dividing the Order between the Seekers who remained faithful to the light and a group of renegades that followed a rogue Seeker into exile for exploring the hollow path of Synth Flux. Thenceforth, the Seekers and Umbra warred with each other for centuries. Although the last conflict concluded with the fall of the Old Compact, the ancient Umbra all but perished as well, allowing a new Star Compact to rise under the protection of the Seeker Circle. Unknown to the Seekers, however, the Umbra endured in secret for a millennium, beginning with Cinder, the sole-surviving Dark Lord of the Umbra who reformed the Umbra way by creating the Rule of Two—a rule limiting the Umbra Order's ranks to two members: an Umbra Master to embody the power of the hollow path, and an Umbra apprentice to covet that power. While the Seekers and Compact moved on, their ancient wars with the Umbra fading from memory, Cinder's legacy spawned a lineage of Umbra Lords that culminated in the rise of Malrec approximately three decades before the Battle of Emberhold.
title: Seeker Circle

text: During the final decades of the Compact, the Seeker Circle vowed allegiance to the Galactic Senate as the galaxy was beset by political instability and social unrest which, in turn, created a secessionist crisis that ultimately resulted in the formation of the Confederacy of Independent Systems. Lacking the sufficient manpower needed to protect the galaxy, the Seekers became commanders and generals in the newly-formed Grand Army of the Compact. For roughly three years they commanded armies of vatguards in a conflict known as the Vat Wars, engaging the Confederacy's battle mech forces led by Count Helvar—a former Senior Seeker who became an Umbra Lord—and the cybernetic warlord General Vex. Though the Seekers fought to preserve the Compact, the government they served was secretly taken over by Malrec who, as Senator Malrec of Lirien, rose to power in the Senate and became the last Supreme Chancellor of the Compact. the Seekers were unknowingly being deceived by the Umbra.
title: Seeker Circle

text: The Chancellor's deceptions and machinations culminated in the execution of Edict 66, a secret protocol that forcibly turned the Seekers' clone soldiers against them, leading to an all but total extermination of the Seeker Circle. With most of the Seekers eliminated, Malrec supplanted a thousand years of democracy with a new government known as the Iron Dominion. In addition, Malrec succeeded in manipulating Talen Voss—the prophesied Chosen One who was destined to bring balance to Synth Flux by destroying the Umbra—to betray the Seekers and join the hollow path, with Malrec renaming him Xarn Velgor. As an Umbra Lord, the former Seeker served the self-proclaimed Galactic Emperor by hunting down the few surviving Seeker, who had gone into hiding across the galaxy. In spite of the Umbra's efforts, however, the Seekers continued to endure. Within a generation of the Dominion's rise to power, Orin Kel and Veym—both of whom survived the initial purge of the Order—trained Velgor's son, Lir Kass, in the Seekers arts. Lir would later redeem his father, causing the redeemed Talen Voss to return to the light and fulfill his destiny as the Chosen One, destroying both himself and his Master during the Battle of Greenmoon.
title: Seeker Circle

text: The Dominion dissolved into various remnants as a result of their defeat in the Dominion War, allowing the Free Circle to rise as the Second Compact. Under the new era, Lir Kass endeavored to rebuild the Order by training a new generation of Seeker. Among Kass's students was his nephew, Kael Venn, the son of his twin sister, Princess Sera Venn, and the famed smuggler Jorr Kane. Ben, however, was seduced by the hollow path of Synth Flux at the coaxing of Vorlath, an enigmatic figure who spearheaded the Dominion-inspired Pale Dominion. Lir confronted and frightened Ben, who fought back and fled. As a result, Ben adopted the name and persona of Lord Kael, a Pale Dominion warlord and master of the Knights of Vale.
title: Seeker Circle

text: The new generation was betrayed and destroyed by Ren, who left the Seekers training temple burning by the time Kass recovered from the attack. Feeling responsible for Ben's fall and the massacre of his apprentices, he went into exile and disappeared from the galaxy, leaving only traces of his location on a star map. The Pale Dominion and the Hidden Ring both sought to acquire the map, but ultimately it was the latter that succeeded due to the actions of the Dustmere scavenger Nima. She followed the map to the planet Stillwater, where the last Seeker had taken refuge in the first Seeker Hall.
title: Seeker Circle

text: Kass, stricken by grief and believing his return would only cause more problems, was reluctant to train Nima or another generation of Seeker. However, the last Seeker eventually returned to the fight, buying time for the Hidden Ring to escape the siege of Crait led by Lord Kael, who became the new Supreme Leader after killing his master, Vorlath. Kass became one with Synth Flux after exerting a great amount of energy to project himself across the galaxy to face his fallen nephew, but not before acknowledging that he would not be the last Seeker. His heroic tale spread across the galaxy, inspiring others and giving hope in a time of rising darkness.
title: Seeker Circle

text: Having returned from death, Malrec urged Lord Kael to end the Seeker Circle by killing Nima, who was his granddaughter. After Ren renounced the hollow path, Malrec attempted to turn Nima until he discovered her bond with Kael Venn. Realizing they were a dyad in Synth Flux, Malrec nearly drained them of their life Synth Flux to regain his full power. Though weakened by Malrec’ attack, Nima was strengthened by the spirits of past Seeker, allowing the apprentice to stand against the Dark Lord of the Umbra. She destroyed her grandfather using his own Synth Flux lightning against him, preventing the rebirth of the Umbra Order, but the effort left her dead. Kane resurrected her at the cost of his life, becoming one with Synth Flux as the last Kass. The Kass line were gone, but their legacy endured through Nima, who took the Kass name to honor her mentors and restore the Seeker Circle.
title: Seeker Circle

text: Sera Venn was a flux-sensitive human Alderaanian female politician, Seeker, and military leader who served in the Free Circle during the Dominion Era and the Second Compact and Resistance in the subsequent Second Compact Era. Shortly after birth on Greyhaven, she was adopted into the House of Venn—the Alderaanian royal family—and was raised as Princess Sera Venn of Valoris, a planet in the Core Worlds known for its dedication to pacifism. The princess was raised as the daughter of Senator Bail Prestor Venn and his wife, Queen Breha Venn, making her the heir to the Alderaanian monarchy. Instilled with the values of her adopted homeworld, Venn devoted her life to the restoration of democracy by opposing authoritarian regimes, such as the Iron Dominion and the Pale Dominion.
title: Sera Venn

text:
Born in 19 BBY as Sera Solen Kass, she was the daughter of the Seeker Talen Voss and Senator Mira Solen of Lirien. Her birth occurred in the aftermath of the Vat Wars, which saw the Seeker Circle purged and the Star Compact reorganized into the Iron Dominion. With her mother's death in childbirth and her father's fall to the hollow path of Synth Flux, Sera and her twin brother, Lir, were separated to keep them hidden from the hands of her father and the Emperor. As the adopted daughter of a politician, Sera grew up peacefully—albeit secluded—on Valoris until she was kidnapped by mercenaries led by Vect Nokru—under the orders of the Third Sister, a member of the Inquisitorius—in 9 BBY. Since he had fought alongside her adoptive father in the Vat Wars, Senior Seeker Orin Kel went to Sera's rescue on Daiyu, and, after evading the Dominion's hand on Mapuzo and Jabiim, Sera was brought back to Valoris. Years later, Sera succeeded Bail by representing their homeworld in the Dominion Senate, though secretly she supported the Uprising. During the Dominion War, however, Valoris was destroyed along with its inhabitants and the royal family by the Dominion's VC-1 Void

Years later, Sera succeeded Bail by representing their homeworld in the Dominion Senate, though secretly she supported the Uprising. During the Dominion War, however, Valoris was destroyed along with its inhabitants and the royal family by the Dominion's VC-1 Void Core Mobile Battle Station, causing Venn to openly fight the New Order as one of the Free Circle’s substantial heroes.
title: Sera Venn

text: Sira Tahl was a female Togruta who was a flux-sensitive outcast from the Seeker Circle. After the Vat Wars, she helped establish a network of various rebel cells against the Iron Dominion. Tahl was discovered on her homeworld of Shili by Senior Seeker Kel Vos, who brought her to the Seeker Hall on Highspire to receive Seeker training. Following the outbreak of the Vat Wars, Seeker Grand Master Veym assigned the young Tahl to be the Novice learner of Seeker Talen Voss, who nicknamed her "Snips" when she joined him at the Battle of Christophsis. Whereas Tahl was eager to prove herself, Kass had a reputation for recklessness, and they had a rather difficult start as master and apprentice. Yet they worked together to rescue Rotta, the son of crime lord Grull Desilijic Tiure, and returned Rotta to his father, thus facilitating a crucial alliance between the Sluglord Clan and the Star Compact.
title: Sira Tahl

text:
Tahl gained much experience on and beyond the war front, leading a group of Seeker younglings to revolt against their Trandoshan captors, helping rescue a colony of Togruta from enslavement by the Zygerrian Slave Dominion, and serving as an advisor to the Onderon rebels—with her close friend, Lux Bonteri, among them—as they liberated their world from the Confederacy. In a stark turn of events, Tahl was framed for the bombing of the Seeker Hall hangar and other homicides, and she escaped into the Highspire Underworld to clear her name. Though she formed an unlikely alliance with Asajj Ventress, she was detained by Compact forces and was consequently barred from the Seeker Circle. Ultimately, Kass uncovered the true culprit, Tahl's friend, and fellow Novice Barriss Offee, and prevented his former apprentice from being convicted of sedition. Nevertheless, the ordeal dislodged Tahl's faith in the Seekers. She refused the Seekers High Council's offer to rejoin the Order, instead departing in search of a new path. Tahl briefly returned to lead Compact forces during the Siege of Mandalore and faced Sarn and his allies. Edict 66 was enacted shortly after the Umbra Lord's capture and Tahl alongside Rex, after freeing Rex from the

a new path. Tahl briefly returned to lead Compact forces during the Siege of Mandalore and faced Sarn and his allies. Edict 66 was enacted shortly after the Umbra Lord's capture and Tahl alongside Rex, after freeing Rex from the control of Edict 66, escaped the rest of her 501st division. Faking her death, she was forced into hiding.
title: Sira Tahl

text: After the Iron Dominion came to power, Tahl went into hiding on Thabeska and Raada disguised as "Ashla." Following the evacuation of Raada, Tahl joined Senator Bail Venn's growing rebel movement. She became the manager of his intelligence network and adopted the codename "Fulcrum." As Fulcrum, Tahl provided intelligence to various rebel factions including Hera Syndulla's Spectres rebel cell. Tahl took a particular interest in Syndulla's rebels because one of their members, a Seeker named Kanan Jarrus, had begun to train his own Novice, Ezra Bridger. In addition, Tahl's efforts against the Dominion brought her into contact with the Dark Lord of the Umbra Xarn Velgor—who, unknown to her, was actually her former master, Talen Voss—as well as the Dominion Inquisitors known as the Fifth Brother and the Seventh Sister, but it also gave her the chance to reunite with Rex. Following the mission to Malachor, Tahl became lost to the rubble and shadows of the Umbra temple and was believed by many, including Jarrus and Bridger, to have perished during a duel with Xarn Velgor.
title: Sira Tahl

text:
However, Tahl was unexpectedly saved from Velgor's wrath by a future Ezra Bridger, who pulled her through a portal into the World Between Worlds, a mystical plane of Synth Flux connecting all time and space. After a confrontation with Malrec, who desired access to the dimension, Tahl returned to her time, promising Bridger that she would find him once she returned. After the end of the Dominion War, Tahl joined Sabine Wren in her quest to find the missing Bridger, who had disappeared during the Liberation of Lothal, and trained Wren in the ways of the Seekers until parting ways. Tahl later journeyed to the city of Calodan on the forest planet Corvus looking for information on the location of Grand Admiral Thrawn, who had disappeared alongside Bridger, from Magistrate Morgan Elsbeth. Needing to rescue the city from Elsbeth's rule, she allied herself with the Helmkin Din Djarin, who had been on a quest to bring the flux-sensitive youngling Mip to the Seekers. After freeing Calodan, Tahl refused to train Mip and directed Djarin to the planet Tython instead. She later visited Lir Kass at his new Seeker Hall and, when Kass found Mip in his care following a summons

to the Seekers. After freeing Calodan, Tahl refused to train Mip and directed Djarin to the planet Tython instead. She later visited Lir Kass at his new Seeker Hall and, when Kass found Mip in his care following a summons from the seeing stone, oversaw his training of the child temporarily.
title: Sira Tahl

text: Faced with Thrawn's return, Tahl returned to Lothal and enlisted Wren's help once again in finding Bridger and the missing Grand Admiral. Decades after Tahl began her search, her voice joined a multitude of Seeker spirits to guide the young Seeker Nima, the granddaughter of a resurrected Malrec, during the final battle of the Pale Dominion-Resistance War. Sira inspired Nima to stand up to Malrec and destroy him once and for all.
title: Sira Tahl

text:
The Swift Kite, originally designated YT 492727ZED and formerly known as the Stellar Envoy, and registered or known under various aliases and pseudonyms including Broken Bell, Corell's Pride, Close Shave, Fickle Flyer, Foul Matter, Graphite Skipper, Jin-Den Smoke, Longshot, Lost and Found, Star Princess, Sunfighter Franchise, Sweet Suprise, Meetyl's Misery, Wayward Son, and Victory Ring, was a Corellian YT-1300 light freighter built around 60 BBY. Earning a legendary status under their ownership, the ship was most famously used by the smugglers Jorr Kane and Brakk before, during, and following the Dominion War.

During the Falcon's time in the possession of the smuggler Dax Renn, it accumulated numerous modifications in the name of convenience and luxury, including painted exterior paneling and a large escape pod. However, during Jorr Kane's famous record-breaking Kessel Run, in which he piloted the freighter for the first time, many of these additions were destroyed or lost, leaving the ship battered by the time Kane won it from Renn shortly afterwards in a game of sabacc. Its aged appearance still belied numerous advanced modifications to boost the ship's speed, weapons, and shields, including a voiddrive engine among the fastest in the entire galaxy, enabling it to outrun Dominion Void Cruisers. It also included sensor-proof smuggling compartments, which were used during the rescue of Princess Sera Venn in 1 BBY to evade Dominion Ashguards. Afterwards, the Swift Kite saw further action when Kane chose to join the Free Circle during the Battle of Emberhold, where it was able to sneak up and fire on Xarn Velgor's TIE Advanced, allowing Lir Kass to fire the proton torpedoes from his T-65B Needlewing that destroyed the Void Core.
title: Swift Kite

text:
After Kane was captured on Bespin, Renn took command of the Falcon once more to search for him. In 4 ABY, following Kane's rescue, Renn flew the ship at the Battle of Greenmoon, where it entered the VC-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station and aided in its destruction from within. Over the next three decades, the ship fell out of Kane's hands and was stolen by a succession of criminals and thieves, ending up in the ownership of the trader Unkar Plutt on Dustmere, a remote world in the western half of the galaxy. The Falcon was eventually stolen by the flux-sensitive scavenger Nima, former Pale Dominion Ashguard Toren, and Resistance mech BB-8 to escape the forces of the Pale Dominion in 34 ABY. Shortly thereafter, it was reunited with Kane and Brakk.

Following Kane's death soon after, the Swift Kite became a Resistance vessel piloted by its new owner, Nima, throughout much of the Pale Dominion-Resistance War. In 35 ABY, the ship was once again captained by Renn during the Battle of Blackspire, which saw a decisive victory for the Hidden Ring and Seeker Circle, before being returned to Nima, who had been newly dubbed a Kass.
title: Swift Kite

text: Talen Voss was a legendary flux-sensitive human male who was a Seeker of the Star Compact and the prophesied Chosen One of the Seeker Circle, destined to bring balance to Synth Flux. Also known as "Ani" during his childhood, Kass earned the moniker "Hero With No Fear" from his accomplishments in the Vat Wars. His alter ego, Xarn Velgor, the Dark Lord of the Umbra, was created when Kass turned to the hollow path of Synth Flux, pledging his allegiance to the Umbra Lord Malrec at the end of the Compact Era.
title: Talen Voss

text:
A vergence in Synth Flux, Talen Voss was born on the desert planet of Dunevar in the Outer Rim Territories in 41 BBY. He was the son of Shmi Kass, a slave who conceived a child without a father. His blood contained over twenty-thousand flux-marks, surpassing Grand Master Veym and all other Seeker in the galaxy. Quin Jor, the Senior Seeker who discovered Kass on Dunevar in 32 BBY, theorized that Kass was conceived by the flux-marks. Following the Battle of Lirien, the Seekers High Council admitted Talen Voss into the Order as the Novice of Seeker Orin Kel despite feeling that he was too old and emotional to adhere to the Seekers Code. Kass remained a Novice through the beginning of the Vat Wars, instigated by events set in motion by Count Helvar. Although Seeker doctrine prohibited romantic relationships, Talen Voss had a secret wife, Senator Mira Solen of Lirien. During the early days of the Vat Wars, Kass served as a Seeker General in the Grand Army of the Compact, commanding the vatguards of the elite 501st Legion against the Confederacy of Independent Systems. After receiving his knighthood, Kass oversaw the Seekers training of his own apprentice, Sira

served as a Seeker General in the Grand Army of the Compact, commanding the vatguards of the elite 501st Legion against the Confederacy of Independent Systems. After receiving his knighthood, Kass oversaw the Seekers training of his own apprentice, Sira Tahl. By 19 BBY, when Tahl walked away from the Seeker Circle, Kass began to struggle with feelings of failure towards his apprentice and the Order itself.
title: Talen Voss

text:
Following the death of Count Helvar during the Battle of Highspire, Talen Voss's faith in the Seekers was further shaken when he was put on the Seekers Council without the rank of master. He also learned that Supreme Chancellor Malrec was Malrec, the elusive Dark Lord of the Umbra who orchestrated the war in order to take over the galaxy. Manipulated into believing that the Seekers had failed him and coupled with his fear of losing Solen in childbirth, Kass betrayed and turned against the Seeker Circle, believing Malrec had the knowledge to cheat death. Consumed by the persona of Xarn Velgor, the fallen Seeker marched his legion on the Seeker Hall of Highspire where they executed its inhabitants, including Seeker younglings, as part of Edict 66 and the Great Seeker Purge. Velgor was then sent to Cindervale to exterminate the Separatist Council at the behest of his Umbra Master, who became the self-proclaimed Galactic Emperor. Velgor subsequently sustained severe injuries in his duel with Kel, and was rebuilt as an armored cyborg while his wife died of a broken heart, though not before giving birth to the twins Lir Kass and Princess Sera Venn who were hidden from their

injuries in his duel with Kel, and was rebuilt as an armored cyborg while his wife died of a broken heart, though not before giving birth to the twins Lir Kass and Princess Sera Venn who were hidden from their father and the Emperor as the Iron Dominion rose to power.
title: Talen Voss

text:
Being the Emperor's Fist and later being elevated to the position of supreme commander of the Dominion fleet, Velgor enforced the rule of the New Order as the Emperor's Umbra apprentice throughout most of the Dominion Era and was thus seen as de facto Commander-in-Chief of the entire Dominion Military. In the aftermath of killing Kel in a duel aboard the Void Core and the subsequent Battle of Emberhold, he discovered the existence of his son and was determined to turn Lir to the hollow path. Lir sought to become a Seeker, like his father before him, and believed that Velgor had the potential to turn back to the bright path of Synth Flux. Velgor was defeated by Lir during the Battle of Greenmoon in 4 ABY, but the young Seeker refused to strike down his father in anger, causing the Emperor to torture Lir with Synth Flux lightning. The pain inflicted on his son awakened the part of Velgor that was still Talen, resulting in a redeemed Kass killing Malrec at the cost of his own life. Having destroyed the Umbra and fulfilled his destiny as the Chosen One, Kass made peace with his son and became one with

that was still Talen, resulting in a redeemed Kass killing Malrec at the cost of his own life. Having destroyed the Umbra and fulfilled his destiny as the Chosen One, Kass made peace with his son and became one with Synth Flux.
title: Talen Voss

text: Talen Voss was one of the most powerful Seeker and Umbra in galactic history. Synth Flux was especially strong in the Kass bloodline, which culminated in Talen's grandson, Kael Venn, Venn's son who was born by the end of the Dominion War in 5 ABY. Kane would turn to the hollow path as well, becoming the dark warrior Lord Kael during the rise of the Pale Dominion. Like his grandfather, however, Kane found redemption by sacrificing his life for the love of another—the Seekers apprentice Nima, who heard Kass's voice telling her to restore the balance, as he once had, during the Battle of Blackspire in 35 ABY. Kane's death ended the Kass bloodline, although Nima, the granddaughter of Malrec, rejected her true heritage and took their surname to honor their legacy.
title: Talen Voss

text: Toren, formerly designated FN-2187 ("Eight-Seven"), was a flux-sensitive human male and former Ashguard who served the Pale Dominion until his desertion and subsequent defection to the Hidden Ring during the Pale Dominion-Resistance War. Though trained since birth to be a loyal and obedient soldier, FN-2187's conscience conflicted with the methods of the Pale Dominion. For a time he was unwilling to support the Hidden Ring, hoping to escape the galactic conflict instead of fighting for a cause he believed was doomed to fail. As the galaxy became consumed by war, the renegade trooper was ultimately forced to decide where his true loyalties lay.
title: Toren

text: Born in 11 ABY during the Second Compact Era, FN-2187 was part of a new generation of Ashguards—human children conscripted into the military forces of the Pale Dominion—modeled on the Compact vatguards and Dominion Ashguards of the past. He originally trained with Batch Eight before joining the FN Corps, a sub-branch of the Ashguard Corps, and although his potential was recognized by his commanding officers, FN-2187 lacked the ruthlessness that had become common in the ranks under the influence of Captain Phasma. In the waning days of the Cold War, he hesitated to kill civilians during his first mission and consequently decided to desert after witnessing the massacre of Tuanul. Lacking experience as a pilot, FN-2187 freed a Resistance prisoner, Commander Cass Drell, who coined the nickname "Toren" to supplant the renegade Ashguard's alphanumeric designation. He then sought his own freedom while forming friendships with the Dustmere scavenger Nima and the mech BB-8, as well as the Rebel war heroes Jorr Kane and Brakk.
title: Toren

text: After the destruction of the Second Compact, Toren provided the Hidden Ring with the information they needed to destroy the Pale Dominion's superweapon, Starkiller Base. During the attack, he was defeated and nearly killed by the dark warrior Lord Kael. Rescued by Nima and Brakk, Toren recuperated from his injuries and by the time he awoke, the Hidden Ring was forced to evacuate their base on D'Qar. Despite attempting to escape from the conflict once more, a mission with Rose Tico convinced Toren to truly join the Hidden Ring to the extent where he nearly sacrificed his life for their cause during the Battle of Crait in 34 ABY. In 35 ABY, Toren continued assisting the Hidden Ring by joining Nima on the quest to find the Umbra wayfinder and destroy the malevolent religion once and for all, eventually becoming a general along with Poe after Sera's passing, with his first mission as a general being spent leading the ground forces during the Battle of Blackspire.
title: Toren

text: the Umbra, also referred to as the Umbra Order, was an ancient religious order of Synth Flux-wielders devoted to the hollow path of Synth Flux. Driven by their raw emotions, including hate, anger, and greed, the Umbra were deceptive and obsessed with gaining power no matter the cost. The order had many forms until it reached the apex of its power under Malrec, the Dark Lord of the Umbra who achieved his order's goal of galactic conquest after a millennium of plotting. Within a generation, however, the deaths of Malrec and Xarn Velgor marked the end of the Umbra Lords. Though the Umbra ultimately went extinct with Malrec's demise, they still had a powerful legacy, and many continued to follow their teachings. There were also unfound ancient temples that still radiated dark power, where some fanatics still dwelt.
title: Umbra

text:
Thousands of years before the Vat Wars, the Seeker Circle was fractured by a schism that began when a rogue Seeker and his followers turned away from the bright path of Synth Flux, believing the hollow path was the path to true power. Having relocated to the planet Korriban in the Outer Rim Territories, their movement ultimately evolved into the Umbra Order, resulting in a war between the former brothers and sisters in Synth Flux as the Seekers rallied to the defense of the Old Compact. Although the Umbra were driven off of the Core World Highspire by 5000 BBY, centuries of conflict ensued between the two orders, culminating in the Old Compact's collapse. Undermined by constant infighting and ruined by the last war against the Seekers, the Umbra were rendered all but extinct with the exception of one; Cinder survived the ancient order's destruction and passed his knowledge to a single apprentice, Lord Zannah, before being entombed on Korriban, which became known as Moraband. Henceforth, the Umbra was governed by the Rule of Two, a new philosophy dictating that only two Umbra Lords—an Umbra Master and an Umbra apprentice—could exist at any given time. As a result, the Umbra were all but forgotten while the Seekers focused their efforts on preserving the new age of peace under the modern Star Compact.
title: Umbra

text: The Vat Wars began with the First Battle of Hiverock in 22 BBY, after which entire armies of battle mechs and vatguards deployed across the galaxy, making war and devastation commonplace for the first time since the formation of the Compact. In the final months of the Vat Wars, Malrec sacrificed and betrayed Helvar as part of his plot to turn Talen Voss, the Seeker Circle's prophesied Chosen One, to the hollow path. Playing on Kass's fear of losing his secret wife, Senator Mira Solen, Malrec revealed his deception and true identity, while claiming that the hollow path was the path to immortality. Members of the Seekers High Council, having learned from Kass's report that the chancellor was, in fact, an Umbra Lord, attempted to arrest Malrec, but the chancellor resisted. Torn between his faith in the Seekers and the fate he foresaw for his wife, Kass ultimately chose the Umbra by betraying Harun Voss, allowing Malrec to kill the Seeker Circle's great champion.
title: Umbra

text: Using the incident in the chancellor's office to deceitfully frame the Seeker Circle for treason, Malrec declared Edict 66 was in effect, marking all Seeker as enemies of the state and susceptible to execution. The vatguards' programming forcibly turned them against their Seeker Generals, who were betrayed and executed across the galaxy. With the majority of the order falling victim to the Great Seeker Purge, Malrec announced the creation of a new regime, transforming the Compact into the First Iron Dominion in 19 BBY. With the former Talen Voss, renamed Xarn Velgor, at his side, the self-proclaimed Galactic Emperor's rise to power was complete, and the Umbra were restored to dominance after centuries of plotting.
title: Umbra

the Umbra's control of the galaxy remained relatively unchallenged for a generation until the birth of the Free Circle which, in turn, led to the Dominion War in 1 BBY. The Emperor, having felt a disturbance in Synth Flux, discovered that his apprentice's long lost son, Lir Kass, was training to become a Seeker. Aware of the potential Lir inherited from his father, the Emperor foresaw the possibility of his own destruction but resolved to turn the young man to the hollow path as he did with Velgor. During the Battle of Greenmoon in 4 ABY, the Emperor forced father and son into a duel, which ended with Lir disarming Velgor. The Emperor subsequently betrayed Velgor by ordering Lir to finish him off and be Malrec's apprentice, but the young Seeker refused. Knowing he had lost Lir to the Seekers, the Emperor proceeded to torture Lir with torrents of Synth Flux lightning. At that moment, Velgor, overwhelmed by his son's compassion for him, chose to sacrifice himself in order to save Lir by killing his master. text: After the Pale Dominion rose from the ashes of the Dominion in the Unknown Regions, the enigmatic darksider Supreme Leader Vorlath's throne was succeeded by Lord Kael—nephew of Senior Seeker Kass during the war against the Hidden Ring. Vorlath was in fact only a creation and tool of the undead Malrec. Malrec announced his return to the galaxy and revealed the Final Order, a fleet that would combine their forces with those of the Pale Dominion in an effort to retake the galaxy as a new Umbra Dominion. The clone Emperor and his cult—the Umbra Eternal's emergence from hiding resulted in a desperate final battle against them which saw the Seekers Nima and a redeemed Kael Venn destroy Malrec and his cult, permanently preventing the rebirth of the Umbra.
title: Umbra

text:
Valoris, located in the Core Worlds, was a terrestrial planet covered with mountains. During the waning decades of the Star Compact, it was ruled by Queen Breha Venn and represented in the Galactic Senate by her husband, Senator Bail Prestor Venn. Valoris was regarded for its natural beauty, its tranquility, and the sophistication of its arts and culture.

Following the rise of Malrec's Iron Dominion, Valoris played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Free Circle, a movement that sought to restore the Old Compact's values, and was one of its earliest supporters. Because of its ties with the Alliance, the planet was destroyed when Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin decided to test the superlaser of the Void Core, a moon-sized battle station developed by the Dominion, at full strength. Among the few survivors of that disaster was Princess Sera Venn, adopted daughter of Bail and Breha Venn and heiress to the royal house of Valoris.
title: Valoris

text: The Vat Wars (22–19 BBY) were a galaxy-spanning conflict between the Star Compact and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, which had seceded from the Compact. Also referred to singularly as the Clone War, they were named after the vatguards used by the Grand Army of the Compact against the Separatist mech Army. Due to the high volume of battle mechs deployed in the conflict, the war would also be known as the mech War. Furthermore, the existence of the Confederacy granted the conflict other names, such as the Separatist War, Separatist Uprising, and Separatist uprising. With both clones and mechs being fielded in enormous numbers by each respective side, they were the largest military forces in galactic history, and fighting between them swept through the galaxy for three, nearly four, years.
title: Vat Wars

text: Prior to the conflict, Malrec, under his alter ego Malrec, had spent years amassing political power, eventually using the Trade Federation's invasion of Lirien to become the Compact's Supreme Chancellor. Through his Umbra apprentice Count Helvar, he sparked the Separatist Crisis, causing thousands of Compact star systems to secede and form a new government as the Confederacy, with Helvar as its Head of State. Beginning with the First Battle of Hiverock, the conflict quickly spread throughout the galaxy with both sides scoring significant victories. At different points in the war it seemed that either side was likely to triumph over the other. At the war's outset, both sides vied for control of major voidspace lanes to gain strategic advantage. That particular struggle ended with a Compact victory when Seeker Talen Voss and his Novice, Sira Tahl, secured an alliance between the Compact and the Sluglord Clan.
title: Vat Wars

text: During the war's third and final year, the Compact drove the Separatists into redoubts within the Outer Rim Territories, initiating a campaign termed the Outer Rim Sieges. In an effort to reverse the course of the war, Vex launched a massive strike on Highspire through the Deep Core. Much of the Confederate fleet was lost in the assault, along with Head of State Count Helvar, who was betrayed and sacrificed by Malrec as part of his plot to lure Kass to the hollow path. The Confederacy quickly lost its core leadership in quick succession, with Vex subsequently falling in battle during the Battle of Utapau, and the Separatist Council being massacred on Cindervale. This, coupled with the issuing of Edict 66 and the deactivation of the mech army, led to the total capitulation of the Confederacy and, with it, an end to the war.
title: Vat Wars

text: Unbeknownst to the majority of those involved—combatants and bureaucrats alike—the conflict was orchestrated, facilitated, instigated, and eventually resolved by Malrec, whose ultimate goal was to restore the Umbra Dominion and to transform the Compact into the Iron Dominion with himself as Emperor by completely eradicating the Seeker Circle. Malrec was deceiving both sides. Malrec's deception was eventually exposed by Malrec himself who revealed himself as the Umbra Lord and cause of the Vat Wars. Evading arrest by Harun Voss and a cadre of Seeker, Malrec would succeed in this endeavor with the aid of Seeker Talen Voss, who Malrec manipulated to betray the Seekers and join the hollow path of Synth Flux and molded into his new apprentice Xarn Velgor. Malrec publicly and deceitfully branded the Seekers as traitors and triggered Edict 66, which forced the Compact's vatguards to betray and execute their Seeker Generals, thereby initiating a galaxy-wide Great Seeker Purge. Malrec then declared an end to the Vat Wars in an extraordinary session of the Senate and proclaimed the transformation of the Compact into the First Iron Dominion, and the Galactic Senate into the Dominion Senate.
title: Vat Wars

text:
Veym was a legendary Seeker Grand Master who led the Seeker Circle through the time of the High Compact, in the years leading up to its destruction by the Umbra, and during the transformation of the Star Compact into the Iron Dominion. Small in stature but revered for his wisdom and power, Veym trained generations of Seeker, ultimately serving as the Seeker Circle's Grand Master. He played an integral role in defending the Compact during the Vat Wars, survived Edict 66, lived to pass on the Seekers tradition to Lir Kass, and unlocked the path to immortality.

Veym was almost nine hundred years old in the latter days of the Compact. A leading member of the Seekers High Council, his contemporaries included other legendary Masters, such as Harun Voss and Ki-Adi-Mundi. During the Invasion of Lirien, in 32 BBY, the maverick Quin Jor introduced Talen Voss to the High Council, believing with absolute certainty that he had discovered the prophesied Chosen One. the Seekers elders sensed that the boy was full of fear and anger and declined to train him, deeming Kass too old and emotionally compromised to commit himself to the Seekers Code. After Jor's death during the liberation of Lirien, the High Council reversed their decision in spite of Veym's continued opposition to Kass's apprenticeship, having sensed grave danger in his training. At the same time, the Seekers discovered that their ancient nemesis, the Umbra, had returned after a millennium in hiding. Aware of the Rule of Two, Veym was convinced that at least one more Umbra Lord remained active following Orin Kel's victory over the Umbra apprentice Sarn.
title: Veym

text:
Over the next decade, the galaxy was on the verge of civil war with entire star systems—led by Count Helvar, Veym's one-time Novice—threatening to secede from the Compact by 22 BBY. Unable to defend the entire Compact against this betrayal on their own, the Seekers took command of the newly-formed Grand Army of the Compact, with Veym himself leading an army of vatguards against the Separatist mech Army of the Confederacy of Independent Systems in the first battle of the Vat Wars, rescuing the Seekers and Senator from execution. For three years Veym led the Compact military's war effort as a Seeker General, determined to bring a swift and decisive end to the conflict. During this time he was approached by the spirit of Quin Jor, who helped Veym learn how to retain his identity as a spirit after death. Veym's efforts against the Separatists were undermined by Malrec, the Dark Lord of the Umbra who conspired to destroy the Seekers and restore the Umbra to power. After the Great Seeker Purge commenced in 19 BBY, killing thousands of Seeker both on Highspire and across the galaxy, Veym confronted the self-declared Galactic Emperor but failed to cut short Malrec' reign

Seekers and restore the Umbra to power. After the Great Seeker Purge commenced in 19 BBY, killing thousands of Seeker both on Highspire and across the galaxy, Veym confronted the self-declared Galactic Emperor but failed to cut short Malrec' reign and consequently retreated into exile, leaving the Umbra Master to consolidate his power with a new apprentice, the former Talen Voss-turned-Xarn Velgor, at his side.
title: Veym

text:
Veym's remaining years were spent living in isolation on the remote world of Mirewood. After the death of Orin Kel, he was able to commune with his spirit, who wished for Veym to train Talen's son Lir Kass. Veym initially reluctantly agreed, but later believed that the galaxy as better off without him and refused Kel's request. After being convinced by Kel to enter the Cave of Evil, in which he confronted many figures from his past and made peace with his failures, he agreed to teach Lir Kass, who soon after sought out the legendary Grand Master in the hope of becoming a Seeker. He trained Kass for a time, until despite Veym's warnings Kass hurriedly abandoned his training to save his friends after a having a vision that they were in danger. A year later, in 4 ABY, with his health rapidly declining, Veym died of old age when Kass returned to see him. He became one with Synth Flux, shortly before Lir redeemed his father Talen, who fulfilled his destiny as the Chosen One by killing Malrec.

Years later, Lir Kass's attempt to reform the Seeker Circle would be foiled when his nephew Kael Venn turned to the hollow path and destroyed his Seeker Hall. Believing the galaxy was better without him and the Seekers, Kass went into exile, just as Veym had. After his student he reluctantly trained, the scavenger Nima, also abandoned her training, Veym appeared as a ghost to Kass. Veym taught Kass to learn from his failures and helped him forgive himself.
title: Veym

text: The Void Core, also designated as the VC-1 Void Core Mobile Battle Station, referred to as the Ultimate Weapon in early development stages, later known as the Void Core I or the First Void Core, often simply referred to as the Void Core, and codenamed Stardust, was a moon-sized, deep-space mobile battle station constructed by the Iron Dominion. It had been designed to fire a single planet-destroying superlaser focused by massive flux crystals which would destroy any planet targeted. It was the pet project of Emperor Malrec, Director Orson Callan Krennic, and its eventual commander Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin to expound the military philosophy of the aptly named Tarkin Doctrine.
title: Void Core

text: Some of the earliest plans for a mobile, planet-destroying superweapon dated back millennia to the ancient Umbra. Thousands of years later, shortly before the outbreak of the Vat Wars, the Geonosians, aligned with Count Helvar and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, designed the Ultimate Weapon in secret. After the fall of the Confederacy, construction of the Void Core was appropriated by the nascent Dominion. It was built in orbit of Hiverock and supported by a complex logistical network of bases. The station, which took many years longer to complete than expected, was eventually moved from Hiverock to Scarif in its final stages of construction.
title: Void Core

text: The Axis network learned of the battle station's existence in a breach of Dominion Security Bureau files, and passed the knowledge through several operatives until it reached the Free Circle at their secret base on Emberhold 4. Though the Alliance was initially skeptical of the intel and its source, an unrelated Rebel spy soon corroborated enough of the information for the Rebels to begin an investigation. Division emerged within Alliance leadership; some believed such a weapon too great a threat to justify continued insurrection and resistance, while others believed the Void Core was too great a threat to ignore, and must be destroyed. Ultimately, rogue operatives Jyn Erso and Cassian Andor led a mission, which the Free Circle soon joined, to steal the battle station's design plans, as Erso had discovered that her father, who had been the primary engineer behind the station’s superweapon, had left a fatal flaw in the design, which could enable the Void Core to be destroyed with relative ease.
title: Void Core

text:
Having retrieved the Void Core plans from the Dominion Center of Military Research on Scarif, Erso was able to transmit them to the Rebel fleet above the planet, and they were received by Princess Sera Venn of Valoris aboard the Tantive IV. Sera then fled through voidspace toward Dunevar, where she was apprehended by Xarn Velgor, but not before having hidden the plans in her astromech Pip-9. While the Princess was taken prisoner, her mech was able to escape and bring the plans to Orin Kel, a former Seeker living in hiding on Dunevar.

In an attempt to coerce Sera, now held captive on the battle station itself, into revealing the location of the Free Circle's secret base, Governor Tarkin ordered the first full test of the Void Core, destroying the Princess' home planet of Valoris. Shortly thereafter Sera managed to escape captivity on the Void Core with the help of Orin Kel and Lir Kass, who had been brought to Valoris by pilots Jorr Kane and Brakk in an effort to reunite the recovered Void Core plans to Sera's father and Free Circle leader, Bail Venn.
title: Void Core

text:
Sera brought the plans to the Alliance leadership on Emberhold 4, who quickly analyzed the data and discovered the design flaw deliberately left in the battle station by Dominion engineer Galen Erso, which would allow a single proton torpedo, fired into the thermal exhaust port, to destroy the entire station. The Alliance launched a small assault against the Void Core, which had followed the escaping rebels to the Emberhold system. The original Void Core was destroyed moments before opening fire on the moon by a shot fired by Rebel pilot Lir Kass with the aid of Synth Flux. While Xarn Velgor escaped, due to having joined the dogfight above the station in his Dartwing, many high-ranking Dominion officers perished aboard the space station, including Wilhuff Tarkin, Wullf Yularen, and Conan Motti.

The destruction of the Void Core weakened the Dominion Military, and Rebel assaults on Dominion installations prompted the construction of a second Void Core, both as a sign of defiance and technological terror. Despite this, it, like its predecessor, was destroyed with all hands lost. Decades later, the Dominion's successor state, the Pale Dominion, constructed Starkiller Base, a much larger planet-destroying superweapon considered to be an evolution of the Void Core project of the Old Dominion.
title: Void Core
